  48class EMGAnalysisReconstruct:
  49    """
  50    Class for performing reconstruct analysis. Used to initiate motor unit
  51    identification and then the estimation of fibre potentials in relation
  52    to the needle and its eletrodes.
  53
  54    """
  55
  56    def __init__(
  57        self,
  58        emg_data_preproc: EMGDataPreproc,
  59        mu_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitSettings,
  60        recon_settings: EMGAnalysisReconstructSettings,
  61        mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings,
  62        mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings,
  63    ):
  64        """
  65        Initialise EMGAnalysisReconstruct object.
  66
  67        Parameters
  68        ----------
  69        emg_data_preproc: EMGDataPreproc
  70            Preprocessed EMG time series data.
  71        mu_setting: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitSettings
  72            Settings for motor unit identification.
  73        recon_settings: EMGAnalysisReconstructSettings
  74            Settings for reconstruting fibre potential locations.
  75        mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings
  76            Settings used to perform cluster analysis of fibre potentials, to estimate
  77            fibre positions.
  78        mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings
  79            Setting used to perform jitter analysis.
  80
  81        Returns
  82        -------
  83        None.
  84
  85        """
  86
  87        # Set data and settings.
  88        self.emg_data_preproc = emg_data_preproc
  89        self.mu_settings = mu_settings
  90        self.recon_settings = recon_settings
  91        self.mu_cluster_settings = mu_cluster_settings
  92        self.mu_jitter_settings = mu_jitter_settings
  93        self.n_chan = self.emg_data_preproc.n_chan
  94
  95        # Needle model pos in mm.
  96        self.needle = self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_xy
  97
  98        # SNRs: The SNR values for each channel.
  99        self.signal_noise_ratios = np.array([])
 100        # ranks: The rank of each channel on highest SNR.
 101        self.signal_noise_ratios_ranks = np.array([])
 102
 103        # Space for motor unit results.
 104        # Initialise in find_motor_units.
 105        # Fill in additional motor unit data by running fibre_reconstruction.
 106        self.found_motor_units = EMGMotorUnits([])
 107        self.chan_for_find_motor_units = -1
 108
 109        # Initial threshold for 2D peak detection,
 110        # when detecting multiple peaks.
 111        self.threshold = 0.15
 112
 113    def _calculate_SNR_ranks(self):
 114        """
 115        Calculate the signal to noise ratios and rank them
 116
 117        Parameters
 118        ----------
 119        None.
 120
 121        Returns
 122        -------
 123        None.
 124
 125        """
 126
 127        # Set up vector for signal to noise ratios for each channel.
 128        self.signal_noise_ratios = np.zeros(self.n_chan)
 129
 130        # Calculate SNR for each good channel.
 131        for channel in range(self.n_chan):
 132            # Skip "bad" channels
 133            if self.emg_data_preproc.chan.analyse_chan[channel]:
 134                temp = self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts[channel, :]
 135                self.signal_noise_ratios[channel] = np.mean(temp[temp > 0])
 136
 137        # Sort SNRs in decending order.
 138        self.signal_noise_ratios_ranks = np.argsort(-self.signal_noise_ratios)
 139
 140    def find_motor_units(self):
 141        """
 142        Finds the motor units and records results in mup_t_idx and mu_numbers
 143        mu_numbers are the motor unit labels, 0, 1, 2, ...
 144          these numbers are also the indices used when the motor units are stored in
 145          the EMGMotorUnits object
 146        mup_t_idx are the motor unit potential time indices to retreive data
 147          from the used signal data
 148
 149        Parameters
 150        ----------
 151        None.
 152
 153        Returns
 154        -------
 155        None.
 156
 157        """
 158
 159        # Order by highest Signal to Noise Ratio.
 160        self._calculate_SNR_ranks()
 161
 162        fs = self.emg_data_preproc.fs
 163
 164        # Find all MUAPs in channel with best signal.
 165        if self.signal_noise_ratios[self.signal_noise_ratios_ranks[0]] > 0:
 166            sig_ind = self.signal_noise_ratios_ranks[0]
 167        else:
 168            raise Exception("Sorry, no channels with a calculable signal to noise ratio!")
 169
 170        # Store channel for plots
 171        self.chan_for_find_motor_units = sig_ind
 172
 173        # Apply Multi-dimensional TK operator (Teager-Kaiser)
 174        # to return MUPs in channel.
 175
 176        # Deep copy to ensure processing in TK_filter is not stored.
 177        used_data = self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts[sig_ind, :].copy()
 178
 179        mup_t_idx, mu_numbers = tk.TK_filter(
 180            used_data,
 181            fs,
 182            self.mu_settings.tk_filt_thres_spike,
 183            self.mu_settings.tk_filt_thres_PsC,
 184        )
 185
 186        print(
 187            "Motor Units found: " + str(np.max(mu_numbers) + 1) + " via channel: " + str(sig_ind)
 188        )
 189
 190        # Add motor unit objects.
 191        self._add_motor_units(mup_t_idx, mu_numbers)
 192
 193    def _add_motor_units(
 194        self, mup_t_idx: npt.NDArray[np.int64], mu_numbers: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
 195    ):
 196        """
 197        Adds the motor units as stored objects.
 198
 199        Parameters
 200        ----------
 201        mup_t_idx : npt.NDArray[np.int64]
 202            Time indices for the signal data for each MUP.
 203        mu_numbers : npt.NDArray[np.int64]
 204            Corresponding vector for the above stating which motor unit
 205            the MUP belongs to.
 206
 207        Returns
 208        -------
 209        None.
 210
 211        """
 212
 213        # Create motor unit objects for each motor unit.
 214        # Motor unit numbers are used as a labels.
 215        all_motor_units = []
 216        for i in range(np.max(mu_numbers) + 1):
 217            motor_unit = EMGMotorUnit(
 218                i,
 219                mup_t_idx[mu_numbers == i],
 220                self.emg_data_preproc.fs,
 221                self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_xy,
 222            )
 223            all_motor_units.append(motor_unit)
 224
 225        self.found_motor_units = EMGMotorUnits(all_motor_units)
 226
 227    def _get_motor_units_dict(self, include_settings: bool = False) -> dict:
 228        """
 229        Returns dictionary of found motor units.
 230
 231        Parameters
 232        ----------
 233        None
 234
 235        Returns
 236        -------
 237        dict
 238
 239        """
 240
 241        numbers_motor_units = []
 242        mup_potentials_t_idx_all_motor_units = []
 243
 244        # Create data to save in dictionary.
 245        for mu in self.found_motor_units.motor_units:
 246            numbers_motor_units.append(mu.motor_unit_number)
 247            mup_potentials_t_idx_all_motor_units.append(mu.potentials_t_idx.tolist())
 248
 249        # Define motor units dictionary.
 250        motor_units_dict = {
 251            "numbers": numbers_motor_units,
 252            "mup_potentials_t_idx": mup_potentials_t_idx_all_motor_units,
 253            "fs": self.emg_data_preproc.fs,
 254        }
 255
 256        # Add motor unit settings if req'd.
 257        if include_settings:
 258            motor_units_dict["mu_settings"] = self.mu_settings
 259
 260        return motor_units_dict

 262    def save_motor_units(self, filename: str, include_settings: bool = False):
 263        """
 264        Saves motor unit data so that it can be loaded without recalculating
 265
 266        Parameters
 267        ----------
 268        filename: string
 269            Name of file to save in.
 270        include_settings: bool, optional
 271            Whether to include motor unit settings or not. The default is False.
 272
 273        Returns
 274        -------
 275        None.
 276
 277        """
 278
 279        # Define dictionary to save results.
 280        motor_units_dict = self._get_motor_units_dict(include_settings)
 281
 282        # Convert and write JSON object to file.
 283        with open(filename, "w") as outfile:
 284            json.dump(motor_units_dict, outfile)
 285
 286    def _set_motor_units_from_dict(self, motor_units_dict: dict):
 287        """
 288        Sets motor unit results from loaded dictionary.
 289
 290        Parameters
 291        ----------
 292        motor_units_dict : dict
 293            Dictionary containing saved results of motor unit identification.
 294
 295        Returns
 296        -------
 297        None.
 298
 299        """
 300
 301        # Set sampling frequency of data.
 302        self.emg_data_preproc.fs = motor_units_dict["fs"]
 303
 304        # Load motor unit settings if they were saved.
 305        if "mu_settings" in motor_units_dict:
 306            self.mu_settings = motor_units_dict["mu_settings"]
 307
 308        # Get saved motor units with corresponding MUP.
 309        numbers_motor_units = motor_units_dict["numbers"]
 310        mup_potentials_t_idx_all_motor_units = motor_units_dict["mup_potentials_t_idx"]
 311
 312        # Create motor unit objects for each motor unit.
 313        all_motor_units = []
 314        for i in range(len(numbers_motor_units)):
 315            motor_unit = EMGMotorUnit(
 316                numbers_motor_units[i],
 317                np.array(mup_potentials_t_idx_all_motor_units[i]),
 318                self.emg_data_preproc.fs,
 319                self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_xy,
 320            )
 321            all_motor_units.append(motor_unit)
 322
 323        self.found_motor_units = EMGMotorUnits(all_motor_units)
 324

 698    def save_all_results_and_settings(self, filename: str, save_all_spikes: bool = False):
 699        """
 700        Saves all analysis results and settings.
 701
 702        Parameters
 703        ----------
 704        filename: str
 705            Name of file to save results and settings in.
 706        save_all_spikes : bool, optional
 707            Whether to save all_spikes. Uses a lot of data and is not necessary,
 708            unless plot_jitter_fibre_pair_EMG_and_times is needed.
 709            The default is False.
 710
 711        Returns
 712        -------
 713        None.
 714
 715        """
 716
 717        # Define all results and settings dictionary.
 718        all_results_and_settings_dict = {
 719            "emg_info": self.emg_data_preproc.get_emg_info_dict(),
 720            "preproc_settings": self.emg_data_preproc.preproc_settings.get_settings_dict(),
 721            "mu_settings": self.mu_settings.get_settings_dict(),
 722            "recon_settings": self.recon_settings.get_settings_dict(),
 723            "mu_cluster_settings": self.mu_cluster_settings.get_settings_dict(),
 724            "mu_jitter_settings": self.mu_jitter_settings.get_settings_dict(),
 725            "motor_units_results": self._get_motor_units_dict(),
 726            "localisation_results": self._get_localisation_results_dict(save_all_spikes),
 727            "clustering_results": self._get_clustering_results_dict(),
 728            "jitter_results": self._get_jitter_results_dict(),
 729        }
 730
 731        # Convert and write JSON object to file.
 732        with open(filename, "w") as outfile:
 733            json.dump(all_results_and_settings_dict, outfile)
 734
 735    def load_all_results_and_settings(self, filename: str):
 736        """
 737        Loads all results and settings.
 738
 739        Parameters
 740        ----------
 741        filename: str
 742            Name of file to load.
 743
 744        Returns
 745        -------
 746        None.
 747
 748        """
 749
 750        # Opening JSON file.
 751        with open(filename) as json_file:
 752            all_results_and_settings_dict = json.load(json_file)
 753
 754        # Set preprocessing info used during preprocessing.
 755        self.emg_data_preproc.set_emg_info_from_dict(all_results_and_settings_dict["emg_info"])
 756
 757        # Set preprocessing settings.
 758        self.emg_data_preproc.preproc_settings.set_settings_from_dict(
 759            all_results_and_settings_dict["preproc_settings"]
 760        )
 761
 762        # Set motor unit finding and reconstruction settings.
 763        self.mu_settings.set_settings_from_dict(all_results_and_settings_dict["mu_settings"])
 764        self.recon_settings.set_settings_from_dict(all_results_and_settings_dict["recon_settings"])
 765
 766        # Set cluster and jitter settings.
 767        self.mu_cluster_settings.set_settings_from_dict(
 768            all_results_and_settings_dict["mu_cluster_settings"]
 769        )
 770        self.mu_jitter_settings.set_settings_from_dict(
 771            all_results_and_settings_dict["mu_jitter_settings"]
 772        )
 773
 774        # Set motor units.
 775        self._set_motor_units_from_dict(all_results_and_settings_dict["motor_units_results"])
 776
 777        # Set localisation results.
 778        self._set_mu_fibre_localisations_from_dict(
 779            all_results_and_settings_dict["localisation_results"]
 780        )
 781
 782        # Set clustering results.
 783        self._set_mu_fibre_clustering_from_dict(
 784            all_results_and_settings_dict["clustering_results"], self.mu_cluster_settings
 785        )
 786
 787        # Set jitter results.
 788        self._set_mu_fibre_jitter_from_dict(
 789            all_results_and_settings_dict["jitter_results"], self.mu_jitter_settings
 790        )

 792    def plot_motor_units_raster(
 793        self,
 794        linelengths: float = 0.75,
 795        linewidths: float = 0.25,
 796        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10, 5),
 797        dpi: int = 100,
 798        axis_label_size: float = 14,
 799        title_size: float = 14,
 800        xtick_label_size: float = 12,
 801        ytick_label_size: float = 12,
 802        sort_by: str = "default",
 803        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
 804    ) -> tuple[Optional[Figure], Axes]:
 805        """
 806        Create a raster plot of the potentials of each motor unit in the recording.
 807        Each motor unit is a row in the visualisation, and vertical lines are drawn at
 808        the times of the motor unit's potentials.
 809
 810        Parameters
 811        ----------
 812        linelengths : float, optional
 813            Length of lines. The default is 0.75.
 814        linewidths : float, optional
 815            Width of lines. The default is 0.25.
 816        figsize : tuple[float, float], optional
 817            Size of figure. The default is (10, 5).
 818        dpi : int, optional
 819            Dots per Inch. The default is 100.
 820        axis_label_size : float, optional
 821            Size of axis labels. The default is 14.
 822        title_size : float, optional
 823            Font size the titles. The default is 14.
 824        xtick_label_size : float, optional
 825            size of x tick labels. The default is 12.
 826        ytick_label_size : float, optional
 827            Size of y tick labels. The default is 12.
 828        sort_by : str, optional
 829            How motor units should be ordered.
 830            The default is "default". Options are "default" and "n_potentials".
 831        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
 832            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
 833
 834        Raises
 835        ------
 836        ValueError
 837            Checks motor units are identified.
 838
 839        Returns
 840        -------
 841        fig : Figure
 842            The figure to which the plot belongs.
 843        ax : Axes
 844            The axes to which the plot belongs.
 845
 846        """
 847
 848        if not self.found_motor_units:
 849            raise ValueError("No motor units identified - confirm that analysis has been run.")
 850
 851        # Get motor units and sort if requested.
 852        motor_units = self.found_motor_units.motor_units
 853        sort_options = ["default", "n_potentials"]
 854        if sort_by not in sort_options:
 855            raise ValueError(f"sort_by must be one of these options: {sort_options}")
 856        elif sort_by == "n_potentials":
 857            sort_idx = np.argsort(self.found_motor_units.n_potentials)
 858            # Descending order.
 859            sort_idx = sort_idx[::-1]
 860            motor_units = [motor_units[i] for i in sort_idx]
 861
 862        # Labels for motor units - plus 1 to count from 1, rather than 0, for vis.
 863        motor_units_numbers = [mu.motor_unit_number + 1 for mu in motor_units]
 864
 865        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
 866        if ax is None:
 867            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
 868            fig.dpi = dpi
 869        else:
 870            fig = None
 871
 872        # Time vector for x axis (in seconds).
 873        emg_t = self.emg_data_preproc.get_emg_t()
 874
 875        # Create list of times of MUPs.
 876        # Each entry is an array of the potential times for one motor unit.
 877        potential_t = []
 878        for mu in motor_units:
 879            potential_t.append(emg_t[mu.potentials_t_idx])
 880
 881        # Raster plot.
 882        # Places first motor unit at the top of the plot.
 883        ax.invert_yaxis()
 884        ax.eventplot(potential_t, linelengths=linelengths, linewidths=linewidths, colors="black")
 885
 886        # Axis ticks and labels
 887
 888        # y axis
 889        n_motor_units = self.found_motor_units.n_motor_units
 890        # eventplot starts ticks at 0 if there are multiple motor units, but 1 if there
 891        # is only one motor unit - need to adjust tick locations accordingly
 892        if n_motor_units == 1:
 893            ax.set_yticks(np.arange(n_motor_units) + 1)
 894        else:
 895            ax.set_yticks(np.arange(n_motor_units))
 896        ax.set_yticklabels(["MU " + str(i) for i in motor_units_numbers])
 897        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=ytick_label_size)
 898
 899        # x axis
 900        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=xtick_label_size)
 901        ax.set_xlabel("time (mm:ss)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
 902        ax.set_xlim(min(emg_t) - 1 / self.emg_data_preproc.fs, max(emg_t))
 903
 904        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(self._seconds_axis_label_formatter))
 905
 906        # title
 907        ax.set_title(
 908            "Times of motor unit potentials in the EMG recording",
 909            fontsize=title_size,
 910            fontweight="bold",
 911        )
 912
 913        return fig, ax
 914
 915    def _seconds_axis_label_formatter(self, time_s, pos) -> str:
 916        """
 917        Formatter for matplotlib axis tick labels - will convert seconds to display as
 918        mm:ss.
 919
 920        Returns
 921        -------
 922        str
 923            Formatted string for tick labels.
 924
 925        """
 926
 927        S_TO_MIN = 60
 928
 929        # Number of minutes and seconds for label
 930        n_min = int(time_s / S_TO_MIN)
 931        n_sec = time_s - (n_min * S_TO_MIN)
 932
 933        # Ignore ms if whole number of seconds
 934        # (allow small differences in case of floating point errors)
 935        if abs(int(time_s) - time_s) < 1e-10:
 936            time_label = f"{n_min:02d}:{int(n_sec):02d}"
 937        else:  # include ms
 938            time_label = f"{n_min:02d}:{round(n_sec,2):0{2+3}.{2}f}"
 939
 940        return time_label
 941
 942    def _get_potentials_data_of_one_motor_unit(
 943        self, motor_unit_idx: int, n_ms: int = 20
 944    ) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]:
 945        """
 946        Extract the time series of each motor unit potential of the specified motor
 947        unit.
 948
 949        Symmetrical data is extracted around each MUP's onset; total length of each
 950        segment is approximately n_ms milliseconds (may be rounded if cannot match time
 951        exactly given the recording's sampling rate).
 952
 953        If requested segment length overlaps with the ends of the EMG recording, NaNs
 954        are instead returned for that segment.
 955
 956        Parameters
 957        ----------
 958        motor_unit_idx : int
 959            Index of motor unit in EMGMotorUnits class for which to extract the
 960            potential time series data.
 961        n_ms : int, optional
 962            Number of milliseconds of data to extract. The data will be centered on the
 963            motor unit potential's onset. The default is 20.
 964
 965        Raises
 966        ------
 967        RuntimeError
 968            Raised if no motor units are stored in the EMGAnalysisReconstruct object.
 969
 970        Returns
 971        -------
 972        potentials_data : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
 973            Time series of each motor unit potential, size number of EMG channels x
 974            time x number of potentials.
 975
 976        """
 977
 978        if not self.found_motor_units:
 979            raise RuntimeError("No motor units identified - confirm that analysis has been run.")
 980
 981        # Calculate number of samples to get before and after MUP onset.
 982        n_samples = int(np.ceil(self.emg_data_preproc.fs / 1000 * n_ms) / 2)
 983
 984        # Get motor unit.
 985        motor_unit = self.found_motor_units.motor_units[motor_unit_idx]
 986        motor_unit.potentials_t_idx
 987
 988        # Get potentials from EMG recording data.
 989        # dimensions are channels x time x MUP.
 990        potentials_data = np.full(
 991            (self.n_chan, n_samples * 2, motor_unit.n_potentials),
 992            np.nan,
 993        )
 994
 995        # Get fibre potential data to return.
 996        for i in np.arange(motor_unit.n_potentials):
 997            # Note that index excludes stop_t sample, which keeps the length to n_ms.
 998            start_t = motor_unit.potentials_t_idx[i] - n_samples
 999            stop_t = motor_unit.potentials_t_idx[i] + n_samples
1000
1001            # Only add potentials within boundaries of the time series.
1002            if (start_t > 0) and (stop_t < self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts.shape[1]):
1003                potentials_data[:, :, i] = self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts[:, start_t:stop_t].copy()
1004
1005        return potentials_data
1006
1007    def plot_average_motor_unit_potential(
1008        self,
1009        motor_unit_idx: int,
1010        n_ms: int = 20,
1011        offset: float = 300,
1012        lw: float = 0.5,
1013        clrs: list[Any] | None = None,
1014        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (7, 7),
1015        axis_label_size: float = 12,
1016        title_size: float = 12,
1017        ytick_label_size: float = 6,
1018        xtick_label_size: float = 10,
1019        dpi: int = 100,
1020        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
1021    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
1022        """
1023        Plot the average (mean) time series of the motor unit's potential. The onset of
1024        the MUP is plotted at t = 0 ms.
1025
1026        Parameters
1027        ----------
1028        motor_unit_idx : int
1029            Index of motor unit in EMGMotorUnits class for which to extract the
1030            potential time series data.
1031        n_ms : int, optional
1032            Number of milliseconds of data to extract. The data will be centered on the
1033            motor unit potential's onset. The default is 20.
1034        offset : float, optional
1035            The vertical spacing, offset, between channels. The default is 300.
1036        lw : float, optional
1037            Line width. The default is 0.5.
1038        clrs : list[Any], optional
1039            List of colours to use for lines. Will be cycled. If None (default), uses
1040            CartoColors Prism colourmap.
1041        figsize : tuple[float, float], optional
1042            Size of figure. The default is (7, 7).
1043        axis_label_size : float, optional
1044            Size of axis labels. The default is 12.
1045        title_size : float, optional
1046            Font size the titles. The default is 12.
1047        xtick_label_size : float, optional
1048            size of x tick labels. The default is 6.
1049        ytick_label_size : float, optional
1050            Size of y tick labels. The default is 10.
1051        dpi : int, optional
1052            Dots per Inch. The default is 100.
1053        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
1054            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
1055
1056        Raises
1057        ------
1058        ValueError
1059            Checks motor units exist and vertical apacing is positive.
1060
1061        Returns
1062        -------
1063        fig : Figure
1064            The figure to which the plot belongs.
1065        ax : Axes
1066            The axes to which the plot belongs.
1067
1068        """
1069
1070        if not self.found_motor_units:
1071            raise ValueError("No motor units identified - confirm that analysis has been run.")
1072
1073        # Offset must be positive to ensure that channels are correctly labelled.
1074        if offset < 0:
1075            raise ValueError("The vertical spacing, offset, must be positive")
1076
1077        # Colours
1078        if clrs is None:
1079            clrs = Prism_10.mpl_colors
1080
1081        # Repeat colours to match (or exceed) number of channels
1082        clrs = clrs * int(np.ceil(self.n_chan / len(clrs)))
1083
1084        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
1085        if ax is None:
1086            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
1087            fig.dpi = dpi
1088        else:
1089            fig = None
1090
1091        # Get motor unit potentials and average (mean).
1092        potentials_data = self._get_potentials_data_of_one_motor_unit(motor_unit_idx, n_ms)
1093        potentials_avg = np.nanmean(potentials_data, axis=2)
1094        n_samples = potentials_avg.shape[1]
1095
1096        # Time vector for x axis (ms).
1097        potentials_t = (np.arange(1, n_samples + 1) / self.emg_data_preproc.fs) * 1000
1098        potentials_t = potentials_t - n_ms / 2  # Center MUP so onset is at t = 0 ms
1099
1100        # Plot each channel's MUP, staggered by the specified offset.
1101        for i in range(self.n_chan):
1102            ax.plot(potentials_t, potentials_avg[i, :] - offset * i, lw=lw, color=clrs[i])
1103
1104        # Channel labels.
1105        chan_y = np.arange(0, self.n_chan * offset * -1, offset * -1)
1106        ax.set_yticks(chan_y)
1107        ax.set_yticklabels(self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_names)
1108        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=ytick_label_size)
1109        ax.set_ylabel("", fontsize=axis_label_size)  # set font for any gui label changes
1110
1111        # x-axis labels and font size.
1112        ax.set_xlabel("time (ms)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1113        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=xtick_label_size)
1114        ax.set_xlim(0 - n_ms / 2, max(potentials_t))
1115
1116        # Title
1117        ax.set_title(
1118            f"Average potential (across time) of motor unit {motor_unit_idx + 1}",
1119            fontweight="bold",
1120            fontsize=title_size,
1121        )
1122
1123        return fig, ax
1124
1125    def plot_all_potentials_one_channel(
1126        self,
1127        motor_unit_idx: int,
1128        chan_idx: int = -1,
1129        n_ms: int = 20,
1130        lw: float = 1,
1131        alpha: float = 0.25,
1132        clr: Any = "darkgrey",
1133        lw_mean: float = 2,
1134        alpha_mean: float = 0.75,
1135        clr_mean: Any = "black",
1136        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (7, 7),
1137        axis_label_size: float = 12,
1138        title_size: float = 12,
1139        xtick_label_size: float = 10,
1140        ytick_label_size: float = 10,
1141        dpi: int = 100,
1142        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
1143    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes, int]:
1144        """
1145
1146        Plots the time series of all motor unit potentials of one motor unit in one
1147        channel, with the mean time series overlaid. MUP onset is plotted at t = 0 ms.
1148
1149        If channel is not specified, the channel used for detecting motor unit
1150        potentials is plotted.
1151
1152        Note that the channel is specified using the channel index (counting from 0),
1153        not the channel numeric label (counting from 1).
1154
1155        Parameters
1156        ----------
1157        motor_unit_idx : int
1158            Index of motor unit in EMGMotorUnits class for which to extract the
1159            potential time series data.
1160        chan_idx : int, optional
1161            Index of the channel to plot. The default is None,
1162            which gives the channel used to find motor units.
1163        n_ms : int, optional
1164            Number of milliseconds of data to extract. The data will be centered on the
1165            motor unit potential's onset. The default is 20.
1166        lw : float, optional
1167            Line width of the individual traces. The default is 1.
1168        alpha : float, optional
1169            Alpha of individual traces. The default is 0.25.
1170        clr: Any, optional
1171            Colour of the individual traces (e.g., as string or RGB tuple). The default
1172            is "darkgrey".
1173        lw_mean : float, optional
1174            Line width of mean line. The default is 2.
1175        alpha_mean : float, optional
1176            Alpha of the mean line. The default is 0.75.
1177        clr_mean : Any, optional
1178            Colour of the mean trace (e.g., as string or RGB tuple). The default
1179            is "black".
1180        figsize : tuple[float, float], optional
1181            Size of figure. The default is (7, 7).
1182        axis_label_size : float, optional
1183            Size of axis labels. The default is 12.
1184        title_size : float, optional
1185            Font size the titles. The default is 12.
1186        xtick_label_size : float, optional
1187            size of x tick labels. The default is 10.
1188        ytick_label_size : float, optional
1189            Size of y tick labels. The default is 10.
1190        dpi : int, optional
1191            Dots per Inch. The default is 100.
1192        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
1193            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
1194
1195        Raises
1196        ------
1197        ValueError
1198            Checks motor units exist.
1199
1200        Returns
1201        -------
1202        fig : Figure
1203            The figure to which the plot belongs.
1204        ax : Axes
1205            The axes to which the plot belongs.
1206        chan_idx : int
1207            Channel used to plot the fibre potentials.
1208
1209        """
1210
1211        if not self.found_motor_units:
1212            raise ValueError("No motor units identified - confirm that analysis has been run.")
1213
1214        if chan_idx < 0:
1215            chan_idx = self.chan_for_find_motor_units
1216
1217        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
1218        if ax is None:
1219            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
1220            fig.dpi = dpi
1221        else:
1222            fig = None
1223
1224        # Get motor unit potentials and average (mean).
1225        potentials_data = self._get_potentials_data_of_one_motor_unit(motor_unit_idx, n_ms)
1226        potentials_avg = np.nanmean(potentials_data, axis=2)
1227        n_samples = potentials_avg.shape[1]
1228
1229        # Time vector for x axis (ms)
1230        potentials_t = (np.arange(1, n_samples + 1) / self.emg_data_preproc.fs) * 1000
1231        potentials_t = potentials_t - n_ms / 2  # Center MUP so onset is at t = 0 ms
1232
1233        # Plot each MUP in specified channel.
1234        ax.plot(
1235            potentials_t,
1236            np.squeeze(potentials_data[chan_idx, :, :]),
1237            lw=lw,
1238            color=clr,
1239            alpha=alpha,
1240            label="_nolegend_",
1241        )
1242        ax.plot(
1243            potentials_t,
1244            potentials_avg[chan_idx, :],
1245            lw=lw_mean,
1246            color=clr_mean,
1247            alpha=alpha_mean,
1248            label="mean potential",
1249        )
1250        ax.legend(loc="lower left", frameon=False)
1251
1252        # Labels
1253        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=ytick_label_size)
1254        ax.set_ylabel("\u03bcV", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1255
1256        # x-axis labels and font size.
1257        ax.set_xlabel("time (ms)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1258        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=xtick_label_size)
1259        ax.set_xlim(0 - n_ms / 2, max(potentials_t))
1260
1261        # Title
1262        ax.set_title(
1263            f"Average potential (across time) of motor unit {motor_unit_idx + 1}"
1264            + f" in channel {chan_idx}",
1265            fontweight="bold",
1266            fontsize=title_size,
1267        )
1268
1269        return fig, ax, chan_idx

1271    def reconstruct_fibres(self, motor_unit_number: int):
1272        """
1273        Fills in fibre construction data and stores it
1274        in the corresponding motor unit object.
1275
1276        Parameters
1277        ----------
1278        motor_unit_number: int
1279            motor unit number used as a label.
1280
1281        Returns
1282        -------
1283        None.
1284
1285        """
1286
1287        # Motor unit for this number.
1288        motor_unit = self.found_motor_units.motor_units[motor_unit_number]
1289
1290        # Save the concurrent signal from all other channels for each spike.
1291        all_spikes = np.zeros(
1292            (
1293                len(motor_unit.potentials_t_idx),
1294                self.n_chan,
1295                self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size * 2 + 1,
1296            )
1297        )
1298
1299        # MU firings count.
1300        t = 0
1301
1302        for t_idx in motor_unit.potentials_t_idx:
1303            # exclude spikes right at the edge of the recording.
1304            if t_idx < (self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size + 1) or t_idx > (
1305                self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts.shape[1]
1306                - self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size
1307                - 1
1308                - 1
1309            ):
1310                continue
1311
1312            for channel in range(self.n_chan):
1313                # Skip bad channels
1314                if not self.emg_data_preproc.chan.analyse_chan[channel]:
1315                    continue
1316
1317                all_spikes[t, channel, :] = self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts[
1318                    channel,
1319                    int(t_idx - self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size) : int(
1320                        t_idx + self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size + 1
1321                    ),
1322                ]
1323
1324            t += 1
1325
1326        print("Motor Unit " + str(motor_unit_number + 1) + ": firings: " + str(t))
1327
1328        if self.recon_settings.mavg_all:
1329            self.recon_settings.mavg_length = all_spikes.shape[0] - 1
1330        elif t < self.recon_settings.mavg_length or t < 2:
1331            # if there aren't enough spikes to model the MU, skip it.
1332            print("Too few firings found to model this motor unit")
1333            return
1334
1335        # The x, y coordinates of the fibre potential.
1336        pos = np.zeros((0, 2))
1337        # Onset indices of the MUPs (firings) relative to the overall time.
1338        mup_onsets = np.array([])
1339        # Fibre potential peak times relative to the onset time
1340        # of the corresponding MUP (in indices units).
1341        fibre_potential_times = np.array([])
1342
1343        # Fibre potential peak channels
1344        fibre_potential_peak_chan = np.array([])
1345
1346        max_signal_id = all_spikes.shape[0] - self.recon_settings.mavg_length
1347
1348        # Loop thro' MUPs.
1349        for signal_id in range(max_signal_id):
1350            sig = np.squeeze(
1351                np.mean(
1352                    all_spikes[
1353                        signal_id : (signal_id + self.recon_settings.mavg_length + 1),
1354                        :,
1355                        :,
1356                    ],
1357                    axis=0,
1358                )
1359            )
1360
1361            # Find peaks in 2D array, channels x time.
1362            sub_clusters = self._find_peaks_2d(sig)
1363
1364            if sub_clusters.shape[0] == 0:
1365                continue
1366
1367            # Each peak found above defines a fibre potential. The positions are now
1368            # calculated (estimated) relative to the needle electrodes.
1369            for sub_cluster_index in range(sub_clusters.shape[0]):
1370                # Ensure we don't get spikes outside of recording duration.
1371                time_peak = np.max(
1372                    np.hstack(
1373                        (
1374                            sub_clusters[sub_cluster_index, 0],
1375                            self.recon_settings.spike_dur + 1,
1376                        )
1377                    )
1378                )
1379                time_peak = np.min(
1380                    np.hstack(
1381                        (
1382                            time_peak,
1383                            self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size * 2
1384                            - self.recon_settings.spike_dur,
1385                        )
1386                    )
1387                )
1388
1389                # Get the mean spikes for the fibre peak amplitude.
1390                peak_electrode = sub_clusters[sub_cluster_index, 1]
1391                peak_start = np.max(np.hstack((peak_electrode - 3, 0)))
1392                peak_stop = np.min(np.hstack((peak_electrode + 3, self.n_chan - 1)))
1393
1394                included_electrodes = np.arange(peak_start, peak_stop + 1, dtype="int")
1395
1396                # Remove bad channels.
1397                good_channels = (
1398                    np.arange(0, self.n_chan, dtype="int")
1399                    * self.emg_data_preproc.chan.analyse_chan
1400                )
1401                included_electrodes = np.intersect1d(included_electrodes, good_channels)
1402
1403                if included_electrodes.shape[0] == 0:
1404                    continue
1405
1406                self.sn = (
1407                    sig[
1408                        included_electrodes,
1409                        int(time_peak - self.recon_settings.spike_dur) : int(
1410                            time_peak + self.recon_settings.spike_dur + 1
1411                        ),
1412                    ]
1413                ).T
1414
1415                self.needle = self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_xy
1416                x0 = self.needle[int(peak_electrode), :]
1417                self.needle = self.needle[included_electrodes, :]
1418
1419                # Non-linear optimisation algorithm for fibre positioning.
1420                opt_paras = opt.fmin(
1421                    self._deconv_wrapper,
1422                    x0=x0,
1423                    maxiter=self.recon_settings.max_opt_iterations,
1424                    full_output=False,
1425                    xtol=self.recon_settings.xtol,
1426                    ftol=self.recon_settings.ftol,
1427                    disp=False,
1428                )
1429
1430                pos = np.vstack((pos, opt_paras))
1431
1432                mup_onsets = np.append(mup_onsets, motor_unit.potentials_t_idx[signal_id])
1433
1434                # Add fibre potential times, these are already adjusted
1435                #  and relative to the MUP onset times.
1436                fibre_potential_times = np.append(fibre_potential_times, time_peak)
1437
1438                # Add fibre peak channel
1439                fibre_potential_peak_chan = np.append(fibre_potential_peak_chan, peak_electrode)
1440
1441        # End of signal_id loop.
1442
1443        # Scaling factor to account for tissue attenuation differences in y-axis direction.
1444        pos[:, 1] = pos[:, 1] * self.recon_settings.y_scaling_factor
1445
1446        # Add the results to the motor unit object.
1447        if pos.shape[0] > 0:
1448            motor_unit.add_fibre_localisation(
1449                fibre_centres=pos,
1450                mup_onsets=mup_onsets,
1451                fibre_potential_times=fibre_potential_times,
1452                fibre_potential_peak_chan=fibre_potential_peak_chan,
1453                all_spikes=all_spikes,
1454                generator_potential=np.array(np.transpose(self.opr)),
1455            )
1456
1457        # Restore needle to full needle, rather than subset of the needle.
1458        self.needle = self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_xy
1459
1460    def _find_peaks(
1461        self,
1462        data: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
1463        distance: int = 1,
1464        min_peak_height: Optional[float] = None,
1465    ):
1466        """
1467        Finds peaks in an 1D array.
1468
1469        An alternative is tk.detect_peaks which does exactly the same
1470        as findpeaks in MatLab.
1471
1472        Parameters
1473        ----------
1474        data: NDArray[np.float64]
1475            Data to find peaks from
1476        distance: int, optional
1477            Detect peaks that are at least separated by minimum peak distance
1478            (in indices). The default is 1.
1479        min_peak_height : float, optional
1480            Detect peaks that are greater than minimum peak height.
1481            The default is None.
1482
1483        Returns
1484        -------
1485        peaks: NDArray[np.int64]
1486            Indices of peaks that satisfies conditions.
1487
1488        """
1489
1490        peaks, _ = sg.find_peaks(data, height=min_peak_height, distance=distance)
1491        return peaks
1492        # return tk.detect_peaks(data, mph=min_peak_height, mpd=distance)
1493
1494    def _find_peaks_2d(self, sig: npt.NDArray[np.float64]) -> npt.NDArray[np.int64]:
1495        """
1496        Finds local maxima of a 2-dimensional image area
1497        Dependent on findpeaks algorithm from findpeaks package.
1498
1499        Parameters
1500        ----------
1501        signal: npt.NDArray[np.float64]
1502            Array (n by m) of signal data.
1503
1504        Returns
1505        -------
1506        locs: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
1507            2D array of location of peaks.
1508        """
1509
1510        threshold = self.threshold
1511        base = sig
1512
1513        # Absolute value of signal to account for fibre potentials that are dips.
1514        base = np.abs(base)
1515
1516        sigma = (
1517            self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_sigma_chns,
1518            self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_sigma_time,
1519        )
1520        im2 = np.abs(
1521            gaussian_filter(base, sigma, truncate=self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_truncate)
1522        )
1523
1524        # Apply tophat transform if req'd.
1525        if self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_use_tophat:
1526            im2 = morphology.white_tophat(
1527                im2, morphology.disk(self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_tophat_disk_radius)
1528            )
1529
1530        # Extract each blob
1531        locs = np.array([])
1532        found = False
1533        parse_limit = 0
1534        im2_max = np.max(im2)
1535        # Returns minimum number of peaks only if a suitable threshold exists.
1536        min_number_of_peaks = self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_min_peaks
1537        max_number_of_peaks = self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_max_peaks
1538        prev_n_peaks = 0
1539
1540        # Initial set up for peak finding.
1541        neighborhood_size = (
1542            self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_neighbour_chns,
1543            self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_neighbour_time,
1544        )
1545        data_max = filters.maximum_filter(im2, neighborhood_size)
1546        maxima_init = im2 == data_max
1547        data_min = filters.minimum_filter(im2, neighborhood_size)
1548
1549        diff = data_max - data_min
1550
1551        # Adjust threshold up and down to try and get between the min and max
1552        # number of desired peaks, strictly less than the max, but may be less
1553        # than the min.
1554        while not found:
1555            parse_limit = parse_limit + 1
1556
1557            # Get number of peaks for this threshold.
1558            maxima = maxima_init.copy()
1559
1560            # Remove values below threshold.
1561            maxima[(diff > (im2_max * threshold)) == 0] = 0
1562
1563            labeled, _ = ndimage.label(maxima)
1564            slices = ndimage.find_objects(labeled)
1565            n_peaks = len(slices)
1566
1567            if n_peaks < min_number_of_peaks and prev_n_peaks <= max_number_of_peaks:
1568                threshold = threshold - 0.01
1569            elif n_peaks > max_number_of_peaks:
1570                threshold = threshold + 0.01
1571            else:
1572                found = True
1573                # Save nice threshold for next time to perhaps speed it up.
1574                self.threshold = threshold
1575
1576            # Failed to find suitable number of peaks.
1577            if threshold <= 0.00 or threshold > 1 or parse_limit > 50:
1578                locs = np.array([])
1579                found = True
1580
1581            prev_n_peaks = n_peaks
1582
1583        # Get final locations.
1584        if n_peaks > 0 and n_peaks <= max_number_of_peaks:
1585            x, y = [], []
1586
1587            for dy, dx in slices:
1588                x_center = (dx.start + dx.stop - 1) / 2
1589                x.append(x_center)
1590                y_center = (dy.start + dy.stop - 1) / 2
1591                y.append(y_center)
1592
1593            locs = np.vstack((x, y)).T
1594
1595            locs[locs[:, 1] < 0, 1] = 0
1596
1597        return locs
1598
1599    def _deconv_wrapper(self, loc: npt.NDArray[np.float64]) -> float:
1600        """
1601        Deconvolution
1602        Now reconstruct without using gn!
1603        Calculate deconvolution for each channel in a 50x50 grid
1604        Region is 0-1000u (Y) and 100-500u (X)
1605        Error is abs mismatch across the reconstructions of 'gn'
1606        Calculated as the max variance across the centre of the 5 reconstructions.
1607        This example is a blind hunt across 2500 locations near the needle.
1608        Here, cn is 400 samples long so that a Toeplitz matrix can be created.
1609
1610        Parameters
1611        ----------
1612        loc : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
1613            Coordinates of fibre potential.
1614
1615        Returns
1616        -------
1617        total_var: float
1618            Total variance.
1619
1620        """
1621
1622        self.no_needle_channels = self.needle.shape[0]
1623
1624        cn = self._calc_cn(loc[0], loc[1], self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size * 2)
1625
1626        iterable = (
1627            self._tconv(cn[:, k], self.sn[:, k], self.recon_settings.spike_dur * 2 + 1)
1628            for k in range(self.no_needle_channels)
1629        )
1630        self.opr = np.fromiter(iterable, dtype=np.ndarray)
1631
1632        total_var = -np.reciprocal(np.max(np.var(self.opr, axis=0, ddof=1)))
1633
1634        return total_var
1635
1636    def _cn_element(self, z: float, channel: int) -> float:
1637        """
1638        Generate element of the cn matrix, row 'z', column 'channel'.
1639
1640        Parameters
1641        ----------
1642        z: float
1643            Distance along fibre.
1644        channel: int
1645            Channel index.
1646
1647        Returns
1648        -------
1649        float
1650
1651        """
1652
1653        dx = np.fabs(self.fbx - self.needle[channel, 0])  # X offset
1654        dy = np.fabs(self.fby - self.needle[channel, 1])  # Y offset of channel i
1655        dz = np.fabs(z - self.isz_half)  # Z distance along fibre
1656
1657        with warnings.catch_warnings():
1658            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)
1659            return np.reciprocal(np.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz))
1660
1661    def _calc_cn(self, fbx: float, fby: float, isz: int) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]:
1662        """
1663        Channel functions.
1664        Generate 1/r conv functions for coords fbx, fby for each channel.
1665
1666        Parameters
1667        ----------
1668        fbx: float
1669            Coordinate x.
1670        fby:
1671            Coordinate y.
1672        isz:
1673            Index.
1674
1675        Returns
1676        -------
1677        cn: NDArray[np.float64]
1678
1679        """
1680
1681        self.isz_half = isz / 2
1682        self.fbx = fbx
1683        self.fby = fby
1684        cn = np.fromfunction(
1685            lambda i, j: self._cn_element(i, j),
1686            (isz, self.no_needle_channels),
1687            dtype=int,
1688        )
1689
1690        return cn
1691
1692    def _tconv(
1693        self, ifn: npt.NDArray[np.float64], sig: npt.NDArray[np.float64], isz: int
1694    ) -> float:
1695        """
1696        Deconvolution method function
1697        Create a Toeplitz matrix using the trailing 200 samples of cn
1698        First row will have the maximum at index 0, 2nd at 1 .....
1699        Use a Parzen window on the signal. See FFT deconvolution as to why!
1700        Then deconvolve sig by solving least squares problem.
1701
1702        Parameters
1703        ----------
1704        ifn: npt.NDArray[np.float64]
1705            1D array.
1706        sig: npt.NDArray[np.float64]
1707            1D array.
1708        isz: int
1709            Number of points in the Parzen output window.
1710
1711        Returns
1712        -------
1713        rsl : float
1714            Least squares solution.
1715
1716        """
1717
1718        wsig = sg.windows.parzen(isz) * sig
1719        start_pos = len(ifn) - isz - 1
1720        end_pos = len(ifn) - 1
1721        tpl = toeplitz(ifn[start_pos:end_pos])
1722
1723        rsl = (np.linalg.lstsq(tpl, wsig, rcond=None))[0]
1724
1725        return rsl
1726

class EMGAnalysisReconstruct: 
  49class EMGAnalysisReconstruct:
  50    """
  51    Class for performing reconstruct analysis. Used to initiate motor unit
  52    identification and then the estimation of fibre potentials in relation
  53    to the needle and its eletrodes.
  54
  55    """
  56
  57    def __init__(
  58        self,
  59        emg_data_preproc: EMGDataPreproc,
  60        mu_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitSettings,
  61        recon_settings: EMGAnalysisReconstructSettings,
  62        mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings,
  63        mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings,
  64    ):
  65        """
  66        Initialise EMGAnalysisReconstruct object.
  67
  68        Parameters
  69        ----------
  70        emg_data_preproc: EMGDataPreproc
  71            Preprocessed EMG time series data.
  72        mu_setting: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitSettings
  73            Settings for motor unit identification.
  74        recon_settings: EMGAnalysisReconstructSettings
  75            Settings for reconstruting fibre potential locations.
  76        mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings
  77            Settings used to perform cluster analysis of fibre potentials, to estimate
  78            fibre positions.
  79        mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings
  80            Setting used to perform jitter analysis.
  81
  82        Returns
  83        -------
  84        None.
  85
  86        """
  87
  88        # Set data and settings.
  89        self.emg_data_preproc = emg_data_preproc
  90        self.mu_settings = mu_settings
  91        self.recon_settings = recon_settings
  92        self.mu_cluster_settings = mu_cluster_settings
  93        self.mu_jitter_settings = mu_jitter_settings
  94        self.n_chan = self.emg_data_preproc.n_chan
  95
  96        # Needle model pos in mm.
  97        self.needle = self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_xy
  98
  99        # SNRs: The SNR values for each channel.
 100        self.signal_noise_ratios = np.array([])
 101        # ranks: The rank of each channel on highest SNR.
 102        self.signal_noise_ratios_ranks = np.array([])
 103
 104        # Space for motor unit results.
 105        # Initialise in find_motor_units.
 106        # Fill in additional motor unit data by running fibre_reconstruction.
 107        self.found_motor_units = EMGMotorUnits([])
 108        self.chan_for_find_motor_units = -1
 109
 110        # Initial threshold for 2D peak detection,
 111        # when detecting multiple peaks.
 112        self.threshold = 0.15
 113
 114    def _calculate_SNR_ranks(self):
 115        """
 116        Calculate the signal to noise ratios and rank them
 117
 118        Parameters
 119        ----------
 120        None.
 121
 122        Returns
 123        -------
 124        None.
 125
 126        """
 127
 128        # Set up vector for signal to noise ratios for each channel.
 129        self.signal_noise_ratios = np.zeros(self.n_chan)
 130
 131        # Calculate SNR for each good channel.
 132        for channel in range(self.n_chan):
 133            # Skip "bad" channels
 134            if self.emg_data_preproc.chan.analyse_chan[channel]:
 135                temp = self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts[channel, :]
 136                self.signal_noise_ratios[channel] = np.mean(temp[temp > 0])
 137
 138        # Sort SNRs in decending order.
 139        self.signal_noise_ratios_ranks = np.argsort(-self.signal_noise_ratios)
 140
 141    def find_motor_units(self):
 142        """
 143        Finds the motor units and records results in mup_t_idx and mu_numbers
 144        mu_numbers are the motor unit labels, 0, 1, 2, ...
 145          these numbers are also the indices used when the motor units are stored in
 146          the EMGMotorUnits object
 147        mup_t_idx are the motor unit potential time indices to retreive data
 148          from the used signal data
 149
 150        Parameters
 151        ----------
 152        None.
 153
 154        Returns
 155        -------
 156        None.
 157
 158        """
 159
 160        # Order by highest Signal to Noise Ratio.
 161        self._calculate_SNR_ranks()
 162
 163        fs = self.emg_data_preproc.fs
 164
 165        # Find all MUAPs in channel with best signal.
 166        if self.signal_noise_ratios[self.signal_noise_ratios_ranks[0]] > 0:
 167            sig_ind = self.signal_noise_ratios_ranks[0]
 168        else:
 169            raise Exception("Sorry, no channels with a calculable signal to noise ratio!")
 170
 171        # Store channel for plots
 172        self.chan_for_find_motor_units = sig_ind
 173
 174        # Apply Multi-dimensional TK operator (Teager-Kaiser)
 175        # to return MUPs in channel.
 176
 177        # Deep copy to ensure processing in TK_filter is not stored.
 178        used_data = self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts[sig_ind, :].copy()
 179
 180        mup_t_idx, mu_numbers = tk.TK_filter(
 181            used_data,
 182            fs,
 183            self.mu_settings.tk_filt_thres_spike,
 184            self.mu_settings.tk_filt_thres_PsC,
 185        )
 186
 187        print(
 188            "Motor Units found: " + str(np.max(mu_numbers) + 1) + " via channel: " + str(sig_ind)
 189        )
 190
 191        # Add motor unit objects.
 192        self._add_motor_units(mup_t_idx, mu_numbers)
 193
 194    def _add_motor_units(
 195        self, mup_t_idx: npt.NDArray[np.int64], mu_numbers: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
 196    ):
 197        """
 198        Adds the motor units as stored objects.
 199
 200        Parameters
 201        ----------
 202        mup_t_idx : npt.NDArray[np.int64]
 203            Time indices for the signal data for each MUP.
 204        mu_numbers : npt.NDArray[np.int64]
 205            Corresponding vector for the above stating which motor unit
 206            the MUP belongs to.
 207
 208        Returns
 209        -------
 210        None.
 211
 212        """
 213
 214        # Create motor unit objects for each motor unit.
 215        # Motor unit numbers are used as a labels.
 216        all_motor_units = []
 217        for i in range(np.max(mu_numbers) + 1):
 218            motor_unit = EMGMotorUnit(
 219                i,
 220                mup_t_idx[mu_numbers == i],
 221                self.emg_data_preproc.fs,
 222                self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_xy,
 223            )
 224            all_motor_units.append(motor_unit)
 225
 226        self.found_motor_units = EMGMotorUnits(all_motor_units)
 227
 228    def _get_motor_units_dict(self, include_settings: bool = False) -> dict:
 229        """
 230        Returns dictionary of found motor units.
 231
 232        Parameters
 233        ----------
 234        None
 235
 236        Returns
 237        -------
 238        dict
 239
 240        """
 241
 242        numbers_motor_units = []
 243        mup_potentials_t_idx_all_motor_units = []
 244
 245        # Create data to save in dictionary.
 246        for mu in self.found_motor_units.motor_units:
 247            numbers_motor_units.append(mu.motor_unit_number)
 248            mup_potentials_t_idx_all_motor_units.append(mu.potentials_t_idx.tolist())
 249
 250        # Define motor units dictionary.
 251        motor_units_dict = {
 252            "numbers": numbers_motor_units,
 253            "mup_potentials_t_idx": mup_potentials_t_idx_all_motor_units,
 254            "fs": self.emg_data_preproc.fs,
 255        }
 256
 257        # Add motor unit settings if req'd.
 258        if include_settings:
 259            motor_units_dict["mu_settings"] = self.mu_settings
 260
 261        return motor_units_dict
 262

 793    def plot_motor_units_raster(
 794        self,
 795        linelengths: float = 0.75,
 796        linewidths: float = 0.25,
 797        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10, 5),
 798        dpi: int = 100,
 799        axis_label_size: float = 14,
 800        title_size: float = 14,
 801        xtick_label_size: float = 12,
 802        ytick_label_size: float = 12,
 803        sort_by: str = "default",
 804        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
 805    ) -> tuple[Optional[Figure], Axes]:
 806        """
 807        Create a raster plot of the potentials of each motor unit in the recording.
 808        Each motor unit is a row in the visualisation, and vertical lines are drawn at
 809        the times of the motor unit's potentials.
 810
 811        Parameters
 812        ----------
 813        linelengths : float, optional
 814            Length of lines. The default is 0.75.
 815        linewidths : float, optional
 816            Width of lines. The default is 0.25.
 817        figsize : tuple[float, float], optional
 818            Size of figure. The default is (10, 5).
 819        dpi : int, optional
 820            Dots per Inch. The default is 100.
 821        axis_label_size : float, optional
 822            Size of axis labels. The default is 14.
 823        title_size : float, optional
 824            Font size the titles. The default is 14.
 825        xtick_label_size : float, optional
 826            size of x tick labels. The default is 12.
 827        ytick_label_size : float, optional
 828            Size of y tick labels. The default is 12.
 829        sort_by : str, optional
 830            How motor units should be ordered.
 831            The default is "default". Options are "default" and "n_potentials".
 832        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
 833            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
 834
 835        Raises
 836        ------
 837        ValueError
 838            Checks motor units are identified.
 839
 840        Returns
 841        -------
 842        fig : Figure
 843            The figure to which the plot belongs.
 844        ax : Axes
 845            The axes to which the plot belongs.
 846
 847        """
 848
 849        if not self.found_motor_units:
 850            raise ValueError("No motor units identified - confirm that analysis has been run.")
 851
 852        # Get motor units and sort if requested.
 853        motor_units = self.found_motor_units.motor_units
 854        sort_options = ["default", "n_potentials"]
 855        if sort_by not in sort_options:
 856            raise ValueError(f"sort_by must be one of these options: {sort_options}")
 857        elif sort_by == "n_potentials":
 858            sort_idx = np.argsort(self.found_motor_units.n_potentials)
 859            # Descending order.
 860            sort_idx = sort_idx[::-1]
 861            motor_units = [motor_units[i] for i in sort_idx]
 862
 863        # Labels for motor units - plus 1 to count from 1, rather than 0, for vis.
 864        motor_units_numbers = [mu.motor_unit_number + 1 for mu in motor_units]
 865
 866        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
 867        if ax is None:
 868            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
 869            fig.dpi = dpi
 870        else:
 871            fig = None
 872
 873        # Time vector for x axis (in seconds).
 874        emg_t = self.emg_data_preproc.get_emg_t()
 875
 876        # Create list of times of MUPs.
 877        # Each entry is an array of the potential times for one motor unit.
 878        potential_t = []
 879        for mu in motor_units:
 880            potential_t.append(emg_t[mu.potentials_t_idx])
 881
 882        # Raster plot.
 883        # Places first motor unit at the top of the plot.
 884        ax.invert_yaxis()
 885        ax.eventplot(potential_t, linelengths=linelengths, linewidths=linewidths, colors="black")
 886
 887        # Axis ticks and labels
 888
 889        # y axis
 890        n_motor_units = self.found_motor_units.n_motor_units
 891        # eventplot starts ticks at 0 if there are multiple motor units, but 1 if there
 892        # is only one motor unit - need to adjust tick locations accordingly
 893        if n_motor_units == 1:
 894            ax.set_yticks(np.arange(n_motor_units) + 1)
 895        else:
 896            ax.set_yticks(np.arange(n_motor_units))
 897        ax.set_yticklabels(["MU " + str(i) for i in motor_units_numbers])
 898        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=ytick_label_size)
 899
 900        # x axis
 901        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=xtick_label_size)
 902        ax.set_xlabel("time (mm:ss)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
 903        ax.set_xlim(min(emg_t) - 1 / self.emg_data_preproc.fs, max(emg_t))
 904
 905        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(self._seconds_axis_label_formatter))
 906
 907        # title
 908        ax.set_title(
 909            "Times of motor unit potentials in the EMG recording",
 910            fontsize=title_size,
 911            fontweight="bold",
 912        )
 913
 914        return fig, ax
 915
 916    def _seconds_axis_label_formatter(self, time_s, pos) -> str:
 917        """
 918        Formatter for matplotlib axis tick labels - will convert seconds to display as
 919        mm:ss.
 920
 921        Returns
 922        -------
 923        str
 924            Formatted string for tick labels.
 925
 926        """
 927
 928        S_TO_MIN = 60
 929
 930        # Number of minutes and seconds for label
 931        n_min = int(time_s / S_TO_MIN)
 932        n_sec = time_s - (n_min * S_TO_MIN)
 933
 934        # Ignore ms if whole number of seconds
 935        # (allow small differences in case of floating point errors)
 936        if abs(int(time_s) - time_s) < 1e-10:
 937            time_label = f"{n_min:02d}:{int(n_sec):02d}"
 938        else:  # include ms
 939            time_label = f"{n_min:02d}:{round(n_sec,2):0{2+3}.{2}f}"
 940
 941        return time_label
 942
 943    def _get_potentials_data_of_one_motor_unit(
 944        self, motor_unit_idx: int, n_ms: int = 20
 945    ) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]:
 946        """
 947        Extract the time series of each motor unit potential of the specified motor
 948        unit.
 949
 950        Symmetrical data is extracted around each MUP's onset; total length of each
 951        segment is approximately n_ms milliseconds (may be rounded if cannot match time
 952        exactly given the recording's sampling rate).
 953
 954        If requested segment length overlaps with the ends of the EMG recording, NaNs
 955        are instead returned for that segment.
 956
 957        Parameters
 958        ----------
 959        motor_unit_idx : int
 960            Index of motor unit in EMGMotorUnits class for which to extract the
 961            potential time series data.
 962        n_ms : int, optional
 963            Number of milliseconds of data to extract. The data will be centered on the
 964            motor unit potential's onset. The default is 20.
 965
 966        Raises
 967        ------
 968        RuntimeError
 969            Raised if no motor units are stored in the EMGAnalysisReconstruct object.
 970
 971        Returns
 972        -------
 973        potentials_data : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
 974            Time series of each motor unit potential, size number of EMG channels x
 975            time x number of potentials.
 976
 977        """
 978
 979        if not self.found_motor_units:
 980            raise RuntimeError("No motor units identified - confirm that analysis has been run.")
 981
 982        # Calculate number of samples to get before and after MUP onset.
 983        n_samples = int(np.ceil(self.emg_data_preproc.fs / 1000 * n_ms) / 2)
 984
 985        # Get motor unit.
 986        motor_unit = self.found_motor_units.motor_units[motor_unit_idx]
 987        motor_unit.potentials_t_idx
 988
 989        # Get potentials from EMG recording data.
 990        # dimensions are channels x time x MUP.
 991        potentials_data = np.full(
 992            (self.n_chan, n_samples * 2, motor_unit.n_potentials),
 993            np.nan,
 994        )
 995
 996        # Get fibre potential data to return.
 997        for i in np.arange(motor_unit.n_potentials):
 998            # Note that index excludes stop_t sample, which keeps the length to n_ms.
 999            start_t = motor_unit.potentials_t_idx[i] - n_samples
1000            stop_t = motor_unit.potentials_t_idx[i] + n_samples
1001
1002            # Only add potentials within boundaries of the time series.
1003            if (start_t > 0) and (stop_t < self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts.shape[1]):
1004                potentials_data[:, :, i] = self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts[:, start_t:stop_t].copy()
1005
1006        return potentials_data
1007
1008    def plot_average_motor_unit_potential(
1009        self,
1010        motor_unit_idx: int,
1011        n_ms: int = 20,
1012        offset: float = 300,
1013        lw: float = 0.5,
1014        clrs: list[Any] | None = None,
1015        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (7, 7),
1016        axis_label_size: float = 12,
1017        title_size: float = 12,
1018        ytick_label_size: float = 6,
1019        xtick_label_size: float = 10,
1020        dpi: int = 100,
1021        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
1022    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
1023        """
1024        Plot the average (mean) time series of the motor unit's potential. The onset of
1025        the MUP is plotted at t = 0 ms.
1026
1027        Parameters
1028        ----------
1029        motor_unit_idx : int
1030            Index of motor unit in EMGMotorUnits class for which to extract the
1031            potential time series data.
1032        n_ms : int, optional
1033            Number of milliseconds of data to extract. The data will be centered on the
1034            motor unit potential's onset. The default is 20.
1035        offset : float, optional
1036            The vertical spacing, offset, between channels. The default is 300.
1037        lw : float, optional
1038            Line width. The default is 0.5.
1039        clrs : list[Any], optional
1040            List of colours to use for lines. Will be cycled. If None (default), uses
1041            CartoColors Prism colourmap.
1042        figsize : tuple[float, float], optional
1043            Size of figure. The default is (7, 7).
1044        axis_label_size : float, optional
1045            Size of axis labels. The default is 12.
1046        title_size : float, optional
1047            Font size the titles. The default is 12.
1048        xtick_label_size : float, optional
1049            size of x tick labels. The default is 6.
1050        ytick_label_size : float, optional
1051            Size of y tick labels. The default is 10.
1052        dpi : int, optional
1053            Dots per Inch. The default is 100.
1054        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
1055            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
1056
1057        Raises
1058        ------
1059        ValueError
1060            Checks motor units exist and vertical apacing is positive.
1061
1062        Returns
1063        -------
1064        fig : Figure
1065            The figure to which the plot belongs.
1066        ax : Axes
1067            The axes to which the plot belongs.
1068
1069        """
1070
1071        if not self.found_motor_units:
1072            raise ValueError("No motor units identified - confirm that analysis has been run.")
1073
1074        # Offset must be positive to ensure that channels are correctly labelled.
1075        if offset < 0:
1076            raise ValueError("The vertical spacing, offset, must be positive")
1077
1078        # Colours
1079        if clrs is None:
1080            clrs = Prism_10.mpl_colors
1081
1082        # Repeat colours to match (or exceed) number of channels
1083        clrs = clrs * int(np.ceil(self.n_chan / len(clrs)))
1084
1085        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
1086        if ax is None:
1087            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
1088            fig.dpi = dpi
1089        else:
1090            fig = None
1091
1092        # Get motor unit potentials and average (mean).
1093        potentials_data = self._get_potentials_data_of_one_motor_unit(motor_unit_idx, n_ms)
1094        potentials_avg = np.nanmean(potentials_data, axis=2)
1095        n_samples = potentials_avg.shape[1]
1096
1097        # Time vector for x axis (ms).
1098        potentials_t = (np.arange(1, n_samples + 1) / self.emg_data_preproc.fs) * 1000
1099        potentials_t = potentials_t - n_ms / 2  # Center MUP so onset is at t = 0 ms
1100
1101        # Plot each channel's MUP, staggered by the specified offset.
1102        for i in range(self.n_chan):
1103            ax.plot(potentials_t, potentials_avg[i, :] - offset * i, lw=lw, color=clrs[i])
1104
1105        # Channel labels.
1106        chan_y = np.arange(0, self.n_chan * offset * -1, offset * -1)
1107        ax.set_yticks(chan_y)
1108        ax.set_yticklabels(self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_names)
1109        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=ytick_label_size)
1110        ax.set_ylabel("", fontsize=axis_label_size)  # set font for any gui label changes
1111
1112        # x-axis labels and font size.
1113        ax.set_xlabel("time (ms)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1114        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=xtick_label_size)
1115        ax.set_xlim(0 - n_ms / 2, max(potentials_t))
1116
1117        # Title
1118        ax.set_title(
1119            f"Average potential (across time) of motor unit {motor_unit_idx + 1}",
1120            fontweight="bold",
1121            fontsize=title_size,
1122        )
1123
1124        return fig, ax
1125
1126    def plot_all_potentials_one_channel(
1127        self,
1128        motor_unit_idx: int,
1129        chan_idx: int = -1,
1130        n_ms: int = 20,
1131        lw: float = 1,
1132        alpha: float = 0.25,
1133        clr: Any = "darkgrey",
1134        lw_mean: float = 2,
1135        alpha_mean: float = 0.75,
1136        clr_mean: Any = "black",
1137        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (7, 7),
1138        axis_label_size: float = 12,
1139        title_size: float = 12,
1140        xtick_label_size: float = 10,
1141        ytick_label_size: float = 10,
1142        dpi: int = 100,
1143        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
1144    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes, int]:
1145        """
1146
1147        Plots the time series of all motor unit potentials of one motor unit in one
1148        channel, with the mean time series overlaid. MUP onset is plotted at t = 0 ms.
1149
1150        If channel is not specified, the channel used for detecting motor unit
1151        potentials is plotted.
1152
1153        Note that the channel is specified using the channel index (counting from 0),
1154        not the channel numeric label (counting from 1).
1155
1156        Parameters
1157        ----------
1158        motor_unit_idx : int
1159            Index of motor unit in EMGMotorUnits class for which to extract the
1160            potential time series data.
1161        chan_idx : int, optional
1162            Index of the channel to plot. The default is None,
1163            which gives the channel used to find motor units.
1164        n_ms : int, optional
1165            Number of milliseconds of data to extract. The data will be centered on the
1166            motor unit potential's onset. The default is 20.
1167        lw : float, optional
1168            Line width of the individual traces. The default is 1.
1169        alpha : float, optional
1170            Alpha of individual traces. The default is 0.25.
1171        clr: Any, optional
1172            Colour of the individual traces (e.g., as string or RGB tuple). The default
1173            is "darkgrey".
1174        lw_mean : float, optional
1175            Line width of mean line. The default is 2.
1176        alpha_mean : float, optional
1177            Alpha of the mean line. The default is 0.75.
1178        clr_mean : Any, optional
1179            Colour of the mean trace (e.g., as string or RGB tuple). The default
1180            is "black".
1181        figsize : tuple[float, float], optional
1182            Size of figure. The default is (7, 7).
1183        axis_label_size : float, optional
1184            Size of axis labels. The default is 12.
1185        title_size : float, optional
1186            Font size the titles. The default is 12.
1187        xtick_label_size : float, optional
1188            size of x tick labels. The default is 10.
1189        ytick_label_size : float, optional
1190            Size of y tick labels. The default is 10.
1191        dpi : int, optional
1192            Dots per Inch. The default is 100.
1193        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
1194            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
1195
1196        Raises
1197        ------
1198        ValueError
1199            Checks motor units exist.
1200
1201        Returns
1202        -------
1203        fig : Figure
1204            The figure to which the plot belongs.
1205        ax : Axes
1206            The axes to which the plot belongs.
1207        chan_idx : int
1208            Channel used to plot the fibre potentials.
1209
1210        """
1211
1212        if not self.found_motor_units:
1213            raise ValueError("No motor units identified - confirm that analysis has been run.")
1214
1215        if chan_idx < 0:
1216            chan_idx = self.chan_for_find_motor_units
1217
1218        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
1219        if ax is None:
1220            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
1221            fig.dpi = dpi
1222        else:
1223            fig = None
1224
1225        # Get motor unit potentials and average (mean).
1226        potentials_data = self._get_potentials_data_of_one_motor_unit(motor_unit_idx, n_ms)
1227        potentials_avg = np.nanmean(potentials_data, axis=2)
1228        n_samples = potentials_avg.shape[1]
1229
1230        # Time vector for x axis (ms)
1231        potentials_t = (np.arange(1, n_samples + 1) / self.emg_data_preproc.fs) * 1000
1232        potentials_t = potentials_t - n_ms / 2  # Center MUP so onset is at t = 0 ms
1233
1234        # Plot each MUP in specified channel.
1235        ax.plot(
1236            potentials_t,
1237            np.squeeze(potentials_data[chan_idx, :, :]),
1238            lw=lw,
1239            color=clr,
1240            alpha=alpha,
1241            label="_nolegend_",
1242        )
1243        ax.plot(
1244            potentials_t,
1245            potentials_avg[chan_idx, :],
1246            lw=lw_mean,
1247            color=clr_mean,
1248            alpha=alpha_mean,
1249            label="mean potential",
1250        )
1251        ax.legend(loc="lower left", frameon=False)
1252
1253        # Labels
1254        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=ytick_label_size)
1255        ax.set_ylabel("\u03bcV", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1256
1257        # x-axis labels and font size.
1258        ax.set_xlabel("time (ms)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1259        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=xtick_label_size)
1260        ax.set_xlim(0 - n_ms / 2, max(potentials_t))
1261
1262        # Title
1263        ax.set_title(
1264            f"Average potential (across time) of motor unit {motor_unit_idx + 1}"
1265            + f" in channel {chan_idx}",
1266            fontweight="bold",
1267            fontsize=title_size,
1268        )
1269
1270        return fig, ax, chan_idx
