1272    def reconstruct_fibres(self, motor_unit_number: int):
1273        """
1274        Fills in fibre construction data and stores it
1275        in the corresponding motor unit object.
1276
1277        Parameters
1278        ----------
1279        motor_unit_number: int
1280            motor unit number used as a label.
1281
1282        Returns
1283        -------
1284        None.
1285
1286        """
1287
1288        # Motor unit for this number.
1289        motor_unit = self.found_motor_units.motor_units[motor_unit_number]
1290
1291        # Save the concurrent signal from all other channels for each spike.
1292        all_spikes = np.zeros(
1293            (
1294                len(motor_unit.potentials_t_idx),
1295                self.n_chan,
1296                self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size * 2 + 1,
1297            )
1298        )
1299
1300        # MU firings count.
1301        t = 0
1302
1303        for t_idx in motor_unit.potentials_t_idx:
1304            # exclude spikes right at the edge of the recording.
1305            if t_idx < (self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size + 1) or t_idx > (
1306                self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts.shape[1]
1307                - self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size
1308                - 1
1309                - 1
1310            ):
1311                continue
1312
1313            for channel in range(self.n_chan):
1314                # Skip bad channels
1315                if not self.emg_data_preproc.chan.analyse_chan[channel]:
1316                    continue
1317
1318                all_spikes[t, channel, :] = self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts[
1319                    channel,
1320                    int(t_idx - self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size) : int(
1321                        t_idx + self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size + 1
1322                    ),
1323                ]
1324
1325            t += 1
1326
1327        print("Motor Unit " + str(motor_unit_number + 1) + ": firings: " + str(t))
1328
1329        if self.recon_settings.mavg_all:
1330            self.recon_settings.mavg_length = all_spikes.shape[0] - 1
1331        elif t < self.recon_settings.mavg_length or t < 2:
1332            # if there aren't enough spikes to model the MU, skip it.
1333            print("Too few firings found to model this motor unit")
1334            return
1335
1336        # The x, y coordinates of the fibre potential.
1337        pos = np.zeros((0, 2))
1338        # Onset indices of the MUPs (firings) relative to the overall time.
1339        mup_onsets = np.array([])
1340        # Fibre potential peak times relative to the onset time
1341        # of the corresponding MUP (in indices units).
1342        fibre_potential_times = np.array([])
1343
1344        # Fibre potential peak channels
1345        fibre_potential_peak_chan = np.array([])
1346
1347        max_signal_id = all_spikes.shape[0] - self.recon_settings.mavg_length
1348
1349        # Loop thro' MUPs.
1350        for signal_id in range(max_signal_id):
1351            sig = np.squeeze(
1352                np.mean(
1353                    all_spikes[
1354                        signal_id : (signal_id + self.recon_settings.mavg_length + 1),
1355                        :,
1356                        :,
1357                    ],
1358                    axis=0,
1359                )
1360            )
1361
1362            # Find peaks in 2D array, channels x time.
1363            sub_clusters = self._find_peaks_2d(sig)
1364
1365            if sub_clusters.shape[0] == 0:
1366                continue
1367
1368            # Each peak found above defines a fibre potential. The positions are now
1369            # calculated (estimated) relative to the needle electrodes.
1370            for sub_cluster_index in range(sub_clusters.shape[0]):
1371                # Ensure we don't get spikes outside of recording duration.
1372                time_peak = np.max(
1373                    np.hstack(
1374                        (
1375                            sub_clusters[sub_cluster_index, 0],
1376                            self.recon_settings.spike_dur + 1,
1377                        )
1378                    )
1379                )
1380                time_peak = np.min(
1381                    np.hstack(
1382                        (
1383                            time_peak,
1384                            self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size * 2
1385                            - self.recon_settings.spike_dur,
1386                        )
1387                    )
1388                )
1389
1390                # Get the mean spikes for the fibre peak amplitude.
1391                peak_electrode = sub_clusters[sub_cluster_index, 1]
1392                peak_start = np.max(np.hstack((peak_electrode - 3, 0)))
1393                peak_stop = np.min(np.hstack((peak_electrode + 3, self.n_chan - 1)))
1394
1395                included_electrodes = np.arange(peak_start, peak_stop + 1, dtype="int")
1396
1397                # Remove bad channels.
1398                good_channels = (
1399                    np.arange(0, self.n_chan, dtype="int")
1400                    * self.emg_data_preproc.chan.analyse_chan
1401                )
1402                included_electrodes = np.intersect1d(included_electrodes, good_channels)
1403
1404                if included_electrodes.shape[0] == 0:
1405                    continue
1406
1407                self.sn = (
1408                    sig[
1409                        included_electrodes,
1410                        int(time_peak - self.recon_settings.spike_dur) : int(
1411                            time_peak + self.recon_settings.spike_dur + 1
1412                        ),
1413                    ]
1414                ).T
1415
1416                self.needle = self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_xy
1417                x0 = self.needle[int(peak_electrode), :]
1418                self.needle = self.needle[included_electrodes, :]
1419
1420                # Non-linear optimisation algorithm for fibre positioning.
1421                opt_paras = opt.fmin(
1422                    self._deconv_wrapper,
1423                    x0=x0,
1424                    maxiter=self.recon_settings.max_opt_iterations,
1425                    full_output=False,
1426                    xtol=self.recon_settings.xtol,
1427                    ftol=self.recon_settings.ftol,
1428                    disp=False,
1429                )
1430
1431                pos = np.vstack((pos, opt_paras))
1432
1433                mup_onsets = np.append(mup_onsets, motor_unit.potentials_t_idx[signal_id])
1434
1435                # Add fibre potential times, these are already adjusted
1436                #  and relative to the MUP onset times.
1437                fibre_potential_times = np.append(fibre_potential_times, time_peak)
1438
1439                # Add fibre peak channel
1440                fibre_potential_peak_chan = np.append(fibre_potential_peak_chan, peak_electrode)
1441
1442        # End of signal_id loop.
1443
1444        # Scaling factor to account for tissue attenuation differences in y-axis direction.
1445        pos[:, 1] = pos[:, 1] * self.recon_settings.y_scaling_factor
1446
1447        # Add the results to the motor unit object.
1448        if pos.shape[0] > 0:
1449            motor_unit.add_fibre_localisation(
1450                fibre_centres=pos,
1451                mup_onsets=mup_onsets,
1452                fibre_potential_times=fibre_potential_times,
1453                fibre_potential_peak_chan=fibre_potential_peak_chan,
1454                all_spikes=all_spikes,
1455                generator_potential=np.array(np.transpose(self.opr)),
1456            )
1457
1458        # Restore needle to full needle, rather than subset of the needle.
1459        self.needle = self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_xy
1460
1461    def _find_peaks(
1462        self,
1463        data: npt.NDArray[np.float64],
1464        distance: int = 1,
1465        min_peak_height: Optional[float] = None,
1466    ):
1467        """
1468        Finds peaks in an 1D array.
1469
1470        An alternative is tk.detect_peaks which does exactly the same
1471        as findpeaks in MatLab.
1472
1473        Parameters
1474        ----------
1475        data: NDArray[np.float64]
1476            Data to find peaks from
1477        distance: int, optional
1478            Detect peaks that are at least separated by minimum peak distance
1479            (in indices). The default is 1.
1480        min_peak_height : float, optional
1481            Detect peaks that are greater than minimum peak height.
1482            The default is None.
1483
1484        Returns
1485        -------
1486        peaks: NDArray[np.int64]
1487            Indices of peaks that satisfies conditions.
1488
1489        """
1490
1491        peaks, _ = sg.find_peaks(data, height=min_peak_height, distance=distance)
1492        return peaks
1493        # return tk.detect_peaks(data, mph=min_peak_height, mpd=distance)
1494
1495    def _find_peaks_2d(self, sig: npt.NDArray[np.float64]) -> npt.NDArray[np.int64]:
1496        """
1497        Finds local maxima of a 2-dimensional image area
1498        Dependent on findpeaks algorithm from findpeaks package.
1499
1500        Parameters
1501        ----------
1502        signal: npt.NDArray[np.float64]
1503            Array (n by m) of signal data.
1504
1505        Returns
1506        -------
1507        locs: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
1508            2D array of location of peaks.
1509        """
1510
1511        threshold = self.threshold
1512        base = sig
1513
1514        # Absolute value of signal to account for fibre potentials that are dips.
1515        base = np.abs(base)
1516
1517        sigma = (
1518            self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_sigma_chns,
1519            self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_sigma_time,
1520        )
1521        im2 = np.abs(
1522            gaussian_filter(base, sigma, truncate=self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_truncate)
1523        )
1524
1525        # Apply tophat transform if req'd.
1526        if self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_use_tophat:
1527            im2 = morphology.white_tophat(
1528                im2, morphology.disk(self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_tophat_disk_radius)
1529            )
1530
1531        # Extract each blob
1532        locs = np.array([])
1533        found = False
1534        parse_limit = 0
1535        im2_max = np.max(im2)
1536        # Returns minimum number of peaks only if a suitable threshold exists.
1537        min_number_of_peaks = self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_min_peaks
1538        max_number_of_peaks = self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_max_peaks
1539        prev_n_peaks = 0
1540
1541        # Initial set up for peak finding.
1542        neighborhood_size = (
1543            self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_neighbour_chns,
1544            self.recon_settings.find_peaks_2d_neighbour_time,
1545        )
1546        data_max = filters.maximum_filter(im2, neighborhood_size)
1547        maxima_init = im2 == data_max
1548        data_min = filters.minimum_filter(im2, neighborhood_size)
1549
1550        diff = data_max - data_min
1551
1552        # Adjust threshold up and down to try and get between the min and max
1553        # number of desired peaks, strictly less than the max, but may be less
1554        # than the min.
1555        while not found:
1556            parse_limit = parse_limit + 1
1557
1558            # Get number of peaks for this threshold.
1559            maxima = maxima_init.copy()
1560
1561            # Remove values below threshold.
1562            maxima[(diff > (im2_max * threshold)) == 0] = 0
1563
1564            labeled, _ = ndimage.label(maxima)
1565            slices = ndimage.find_objects(labeled)
1566            n_peaks = len(slices)
1567
1568            if n_peaks < min_number_of_peaks and prev_n_peaks <= max_number_of_peaks:
1569                threshold = threshold - 0.01
1570            elif n_peaks > max_number_of_peaks:
1571                threshold = threshold + 0.01
1572            else:
1573                found = True
1574                # Save nice threshold for next time to perhaps speed it up.
1575                self.threshold = threshold
1576
1577            # Failed to find suitable number of peaks.
1578            if threshold <= 0.00 or threshold > 1 or parse_limit > 50:
1579                locs = np.array([])
1580                found = True
1581
1582            prev_n_peaks = n_peaks
1583
1584        # Get final locations.
1585        if n_peaks > 0 and n_peaks <= max_number_of_peaks:
1586            x, y = [], []
1587
1588            for dy, dx in slices:
1589                x_center = (dx.start + dx.stop - 1) / 2
1590                x.append(x_center)
1591                y_center = (dy.start + dy.stop - 1) / 2
1592                y.append(y_center)
1593
1594            locs = np.vstack((x, y)).T
1595
1596            locs[locs[:, 1] < 0, 1] = 0
1597
1598        return locs
1599
1600    def _deconv_wrapper(self, loc: npt.NDArray[np.float64]) -> float:
1601        """
1602        Deconvolution
1603        Now reconstruct without using gn!
1604        Calculate deconvolution for each channel in a 50x50 grid
1605        Region is 0-1000u (Y) and 100-500u (X)
1606        Error is abs mismatch across the reconstructions of 'gn'
1607        Calculated as the max variance across the centre of the 5 reconstructions.
1608        This example is a blind hunt across 2500 locations near the needle.
1609        Here, cn is 400 samples long so that a Toeplitz matrix can be created.
1610
1611        Parameters
1612        ----------
1613        loc : npt.NDArray[np.float64]
1614            Coordinates of fibre potential.
1615
1616        Returns
1617        -------
1618        total_var: float
1619            Total variance.
1620
1621        """
1622
1623        self.no_needle_channels = self.needle.shape[0]
1624
1625        cn = self._calc_cn(loc[0], loc[1], self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size * 2)
1626
1627        iterable = (
1628            self._tconv(cn[:, k], self.sn[:, k], self.recon_settings.spike_dur * 2 + 1)
1629            for k in range(self.no_needle_channels)
1630        )
1631        self.opr = np.fromiter(iterable, dtype=np.ndarray)
1632
1633        total_var = -np.reciprocal(np.max(np.var(self.opr, axis=0, ddof=1)))
1634
1635        return total_var
1636
1637    def _cn_element(self, z: float, channel: int) -> float:
1638        """
1639        Generate element of the cn matrix, row 'z', column 'channel'.
1640
1641        Parameters
1642        ----------
1643        z: float
1644            Distance along fibre.
1645        channel: int
1646            Channel index.
1647
1648        Returns
1649        -------
1650        float
1651
1652        """
1653
1654        dx = np.fabs(self.fbx - self.needle[channel, 0])  # X offset
1655        dy = np.fabs(self.fby - self.needle[channel, 1])  # Y offset of channel i
1656        dz = np.fabs(z - self.isz_half)  # Z distance along fibre
1657
1658        with warnings.catch_warnings():
1659            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", category=RuntimeWarning)
1660            return np.reciprocal(np.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz))
1661
1662    def _calc_cn(self, fbx: float, fby: float, isz: int) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]:
1663        """
1664        Channel functions.
1665        Generate 1/r conv functions for coords fbx, fby for each channel.
1666
1667        Parameters
1668        ----------
1669        fbx: float
1670            Coordinate x.
1671        fby:
1672            Coordinate y.
1673        isz:
1674            Index.
1675
1676        Returns
1677        -------
1678        cn: NDArray[np.float64]
1679
1680        """
1681
1682        self.isz_half = isz / 2
1683        self.fbx = fbx
1684        self.fby = fby
1685        cn = np.fromfunction(
1686            lambda i, j: self._cn_element(i, j),
1687            (isz, self.no_needle_channels),
1688            dtype=int,
1689        )
1690
1691        return cn
1692
1693    def _tconv(
1694        self, ifn: npt.NDArray[np.float64], sig: npt.NDArray[np.float64], isz: int
1695    ) -> float:
1696        """
1697        Deconvolution method function
1698        Create a Toeplitz matrix using the trailing 200 samples of cn
1699        First row will have the maximum at index 0, 2nd at 1 .....
1700        Use a Parzen window on the signal. See FFT deconvolution as to why!
1701        Then deconvolve sig by solving least squares problem.
1702
1703        Parameters
1704        ----------
1705        ifn: npt.NDArray[np.float64]
1706            1D array.
1707        sig: npt.NDArray[np.float64]
1708            1D array.
1709        isz: int
1710            Number of points in the Parzen output window.
1711
1712        Returns
1713        -------
1714        rsl : float
1715            Least squares solution.
1716
1717        """
1718
1719        wsig = sg.windows.parzen(isz) * sig
1720        start_pos = len(ifn) - isz - 1
1721        end_pos = len(ifn) - 1
1722        tpl = toeplitz(ifn[start_pos:end_pos])
1723
1724        rsl = (np.linalg.lstsq(tpl, wsig, rcond=None))[0]
1725
1726        return rsl
1727

Class for performing reconstruct analysis. Used to initiate motor unit identification and then the estimation of fibre potentials in relation to the needle and its eletrodes.

EMGAnalysisReconstruct( emg_data_preproc: pymicroemg.emg_data_preproc.EMGDataPreproc, mu_settings: pymicroemg.emg_reconstruct_settings.EMGAnalysisMotorUnitSettings, recon_settings: pymicroemg.emg_reconstruct_settings.EMGAnalysisReconstructSettings, mu_cluster_settings: pymicroemg.emg_reconstruct_settings.EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings, mu_jitter_settings: pymicroemg.emg_reconstruct_settings.EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings) 
 57    def __init__(
 58        self,
 59        emg_data_preproc: EMGDataPreproc,
 60        mu_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitSettings,
 61        recon_settings: EMGAnalysisReconstructSettings,
 62        mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings,
 63        mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings,
 64    ):
 65        """
 66        Initialise EMGAnalysisReconstruct object.
 67
 68        Parameters
 69        ----------
 70        emg_data_preproc: EMGDataPreproc
 71            Preprocessed EMG time series data.
 72        mu_setting: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitSettings
 73            Settings for motor unit identification.
 74        recon_settings: EMGAnalysisReconstructSettings
 75            Settings for reconstruting fibre potential locations.
 76        mu_cluster_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitClusterSettings
 77            Settings used to perform cluster analysis of fibre potentials, to estimate
 78            fibre positions.
 79        mu_jitter_settings: EMGAnalysisMotorUnitJitterSettings
 80            Setting used to perform jitter analysis.
 81
 82        Returns
 83        -------
 84        None.
 85
 86        """
 87
 88        # Set data and settings.
 89        self.emg_data_preproc = emg_data_preproc
 90        self.mu_settings = mu_settings
 91        self.recon_settings = recon_settings
 92        self.mu_cluster_settings = mu_cluster_settings
 93        self.mu_jitter_settings = mu_jitter_settings
 94        self.n_chan = self.emg_data_preproc.n_chan
 95
 96        # Needle model pos in mm.
 97        self.needle = self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_xy
 98
 99        # SNRs: The SNR values for each channel.
100        self.signal_noise_ratios = np.array([])
101        # ranks: The rank of each channel on highest SNR.
102        self.signal_noise_ratios_ranks = np.array([])
103
104        # Space for motor unit results.
105        # Initialise in find_motor_units.
106        # Fill in additional motor unit data by running fibre_reconstruction.
107        self.found_motor_units = EMGMotorUnits([])
108        self.chan_for_find_motor_units = -1
109
110        # Initial threshold for 2D peak detection,
111        # when detecting multiple peaks.
112        self.threshold = 0.15

def find_motor_units(self): 
141    def find_motor_units(self):
142        """
143        Finds the motor units and records results in mup_t_idx and mu_numbers
144        mu_numbers are the motor unit labels, 0, 1, 2, ...
145          these numbers are also the indices used when the motor units are stored in
146          the EMGMotorUnits object
147        mup_t_idx are the motor unit potential time indices to retreive data
148          from the used signal data
149
150        Parameters
151        ----------
152        None.
153
154        Returns
155        -------
156        None.
157
158        """
159
160        # Order by highest Signal to Noise Ratio.
161        self._calculate_SNR_ranks()
162
163        fs = self.emg_data_preproc.fs
164
165        # Find all MUAPs in channel with best signal.
166        if self.signal_noise_ratios[self.signal_noise_ratios_ranks[0]] > 0:
167            sig_ind = self.signal_noise_ratios_ranks[0]
168        else:
169            raise Exception("Sorry, no channels with a calculable signal to noise ratio!")
170
171        # Store channel for plots
172        self.chan_for_find_motor_units = sig_ind
173
174        # Apply Multi-dimensional TK operator (Teager-Kaiser)
175        # to return MUPs in channel.
176
177        # Deep copy to ensure processing in TK_filter is not stored.
178        used_data = self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts[sig_ind, :].copy()
179
180        mup_t_idx, mu_numbers = tk.TK_filter(
181            used_data,
182            fs,
183            self.mu_settings.tk_filt_thres_spike,
184            self.mu_settings.tk_filt_thres_PsC,
185        )
186
187        print(
188            "Motor Units found: " + str(np.max(mu_numbers) + 1) + " via channel: " + str(sig_ind)
189        )
190
191        # Add motor unit objects.
192        self._add_motor_units(mup_t_idx, mu_numbers)

def plot_motor_units_raster( self, linelengths: float = 0.75, linewidths: float = 0.25, figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10, 5), dpi: int = 100, axis_label_size: float = 14, title_size: float = 14, xtick_label_size: float = 12, ytick_label_size: float = 12, sort_by: str = 'default', ax: 'plt.axes.Axes | None' = None) -> tuple[typing.Optional[matplotlib.figure.Figure], matplotlib.axes._axes.Axes]: 
793    def plot_motor_units_raster(
794        self,
795        linelengths: float = 0.75,
796        linewidths: float = 0.25,
797        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (10, 5),
798        dpi: int = 100,
799        axis_label_size: float = 14,
800        title_size: float = 14,
801        xtick_label_size: float = 12,
802        ytick_label_size: float = 12,
803        sort_by: str = "default",
804        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
805    ) -> tuple[Optional[Figure], Axes]:
806        """
807        Create a raster plot of the potentials of each motor unit in the recording.
808        Each motor unit is a row in the visualisation, and vertical lines are drawn at
809        the times of the motor unit's potentials.
810
811        Parameters
812        ----------
813        linelengths : float, optional
814            Length of lines. The default is 0.75.
815        linewidths : float, optional
816            Width of lines. The default is 0.25.
817        figsize : tuple[float, float], optional
818            Size of figure. The default is (10, 5).
819        dpi : int, optional
820            Dots per Inch. The default is 100.
821        axis_label_size : float, optional
822            Size of axis labels. The default is 14.
823        title_size : float, optional
824            Font size the titles. The default is 14.
825        xtick_label_size : float, optional
826            size of x tick labels. The default is 12.
827        ytick_label_size : float, optional
828            Size of y tick labels. The default is 12.
829        sort_by : str, optional
830            How motor units should be ordered.
831            The default is "default". Options are "default" and "n_potentials".
832        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
833            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
834
835        Raises
836        ------
837        ValueError
838            Checks motor units are identified.
839
840        Returns
841        -------
842        fig : Figure
843            The figure to which the plot belongs.
844        ax : Axes
845            The axes to which the plot belongs.
846
847        """
848
849        if not self.found_motor_units:
850            raise ValueError("No motor units identified - confirm that analysis has been run.")
851
852        # Get motor units and sort if requested.
853        motor_units = self.found_motor_units.motor_units
854        sort_options = ["default", "n_potentials"]
855        if sort_by not in sort_options:
856            raise ValueError(f"sort_by must be one of these options: {sort_options}")
857        elif sort_by == "n_potentials":
858            sort_idx = np.argsort(self.found_motor_units.n_potentials)
859            # Descending order.
860            sort_idx = sort_idx[::-1]
861            motor_units = [motor_units[i] for i in sort_idx]
862
863        # Labels for motor units - plus 1 to count from 1, rather than 0, for vis.
864        motor_units_numbers = [mu.motor_unit_number + 1 for mu in motor_units]
865
866        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
867        if ax is None:
868            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
869            fig.dpi = dpi
870        else:
871            fig = None
872
873        # Time vector for x axis (in seconds).
874        emg_t = self.emg_data_preproc.get_emg_t()
875
876        # Create list of times of MUPs.
877        # Each entry is an array of the potential times for one motor unit.
878        potential_t = []
879        for mu in motor_units:
880            potential_t.append(emg_t[mu.potentials_t_idx])
881
882        # Raster plot.
883        # Places first motor unit at the top of the plot.
884        ax.invert_yaxis()
885        ax.eventplot(potential_t, linelengths=linelengths, linewidths=linewidths, colors="black")
886
887        # Axis ticks and labels
888
889        # y axis
890        n_motor_units = self.found_motor_units.n_motor_units
891        # eventplot starts ticks at 0 if there are multiple motor units, but 1 if there
892        # is only one motor unit - need to adjust tick locations accordingly
893        if n_motor_units == 1:
894            ax.set_yticks(np.arange(n_motor_units) + 1)
895        else:
896            ax.set_yticks(np.arange(n_motor_units))
897        ax.set_yticklabels(["MU " + str(i) for i in motor_units_numbers])
898        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=ytick_label_size)
899
900        # x axis
901        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=xtick_label_size)
902        ax.set_xlabel("time (mm:ss)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
903        ax.set_xlim(min(emg_t) - 1 / self.emg_data_preproc.fs, max(emg_t))
904
905        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(self._seconds_axis_label_formatter))
906
907        # title
908        ax.set_title(
909            "Times of motor unit potentials in the EMG recording",
910            fontsize=title_size,
911            fontweight="bold",
912        )
913
914        return fig, ax

def plot_average_motor_unit_potential( self, motor_unit_idx: int, n_ms: int = 20, offset: float = 300, lw: float = 0.5, clrs: list[typing.Any] | None = None, figsize: tuple[float, float] = (7, 7), axis_label_size: float = 12, title_size: float = 12, ytick_label_size: float = 6, xtick_label_size: float = 10, dpi: int = 100, ax: 'plt.axes.Axes | None' = None) -> tuple[matplotlib.figure.Figure, matplotlib.axes._axes.Axes]: 
1008    def plot_average_motor_unit_potential(
1009        self,
1010        motor_unit_idx: int,
1011        n_ms: int = 20,
1012        offset: float = 300,
1013        lw: float = 0.5,
1014        clrs: list[Any] | None = None,
1015        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (7, 7),
1016        axis_label_size: float = 12,
1017        title_size: float = 12,
1018        ytick_label_size: float = 6,
1019        xtick_label_size: float = 10,
1020        dpi: int = 100,
1021        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
1022    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]:
1023        """
1024        Plot the average (mean) time series of the motor unit's potential. The onset of
1025        the MUP is plotted at t = 0 ms.
1026
1027        Parameters
1028        ----------
1029        motor_unit_idx : int
1030            Index of motor unit in EMGMotorUnits class for which to extract the
1031            potential time series data.
1032        n_ms : int, optional
1033            Number of milliseconds of data to extract. The data will be centered on the
1034            motor unit potential's onset. The default is 20.
1035        offset : float, optional
1036            The vertical spacing, offset, between channels. The default is 300.
1037        lw : float, optional
1038            Line width. The default is 0.5.
1039        clrs : list[Any], optional
1040            List of colours to use for lines. Will be cycled. If None (default), uses
1041            CartoColors Prism colourmap.
1042        figsize : tuple[float, float], optional
1043            Size of figure. The default is (7, 7).
1044        axis_label_size : float, optional
1045            Size of axis labels. The default is 12.
1046        title_size : float, optional
1047            Font size the titles. The default is 12.
1048        xtick_label_size : float, optional
1049            size of x tick labels. The default is 6.
1050        ytick_label_size : float, optional
1051            Size of y tick labels. The default is 10.
1052        dpi : int, optional
1053            Dots per Inch. The default is 100.
1054        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
1055            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
1056
1057        Raises
1058        ------
1059        ValueError
1060            Checks motor units exist and vertical apacing is positive.
1061
1062        Returns
1063        -------
1064        fig : Figure
1065            The figure to which the plot belongs.
1066        ax : Axes
1067            The axes to which the plot belongs.
1068
1069        """
1070
1071        if not self.found_motor_units:
1072            raise ValueError("No motor units identified - confirm that analysis has been run.")
1073
1074        # Offset must be positive to ensure that channels are correctly labelled.
1075        if offset < 0:
1076            raise ValueError("The vertical spacing, offset, must be positive")
1077
1078        # Colours
1079        if clrs is None:
1080            clrs = Prism_10.mpl_colors
1081
1082        # Repeat colours to match (or exceed) number of channels
1083        clrs = clrs * int(np.ceil(self.n_chan / len(clrs)))
1084
1085        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
1086        if ax is None:
1087            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
1088            fig.dpi = dpi
1089        else:
1090            fig = None
1091
1092        # Get motor unit potentials and average (mean).
1093        potentials_data = self._get_potentials_data_of_one_motor_unit(motor_unit_idx, n_ms)
1094        potentials_avg = np.nanmean(potentials_data, axis=2)
1095        n_samples = potentials_avg.shape[1]
1096
1097        # Time vector for x axis (ms).
1098        potentials_t = (np.arange(1, n_samples + 1) / self.emg_data_preproc.fs) * 1000
1099        potentials_t = potentials_t - n_ms / 2  # Center MUP so onset is at t = 0 ms
1100
1101        # Plot each channel's MUP, staggered by the specified offset.
1102        for i in range(self.n_chan):
1103            ax.plot(potentials_t, potentials_avg[i, :] - offset * i, lw=lw, color=clrs[i])
1104
1105        # Channel labels.
1106        chan_y = np.arange(0, self.n_chan * offset * -1, offset * -1)
1107        ax.set_yticks(chan_y)
1108        ax.set_yticklabels(self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_names)
1109        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=ytick_label_size)
1110        ax.set_ylabel("", fontsize=axis_label_size)  # set font for any gui label changes
1111
1112        # x-axis labels and font size.
1113        ax.set_xlabel("time (ms)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1114        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=xtick_label_size)
1115        ax.set_xlim(0 - n_ms / 2, max(potentials_t))
1116
1117        # Title
1118        ax.set_title(
1119            f"Average potential (across time) of motor unit {motor_unit_idx + 1}",
1120            fontweight="bold",
1121            fontsize=title_size,
1122        )
1123
1124        return fig, ax

def plot_all_potentials_one_channel( self, motor_unit_idx: int, chan_idx: int = -1, n_ms: int = 20, lw: float = 1, alpha: float = 0.25, clr: Any = 'darkgrey', lw_mean: float = 2, alpha_mean: float = 0.75, clr_mean: Any = 'black', figsize: tuple[float, float] = (7, 7), axis_label_size: float = 12, title_size: float = 12, xtick_label_size: float = 10, ytick_label_size: float = 10, dpi: int = 100, ax: 'plt.axes.Axes | None' = None) -> tuple[matplotlib.figure.Figure, matplotlib.axes._axes.Axes, int]: 
1126    def plot_all_potentials_one_channel(
1127        self,
1128        motor_unit_idx: int,
1129        chan_idx: int = -1,
1130        n_ms: int = 20,
1131        lw: float = 1,
1132        alpha: float = 0.25,
1133        clr: Any = "darkgrey",
1134        lw_mean: float = 2,
1135        alpha_mean: float = 0.75,
1136        clr_mean: Any = "black",
1137        figsize: tuple[float, float] = (7, 7),
1138        axis_label_size: float = 12,
1139        title_size: float = 12,
1140        xtick_label_size: float = 10,
1141        ytick_label_size: float = 10,
1142        dpi: int = 100,
1143        ax: plt.axes.Axes | None = None,
1144    ) -> tuple[Figure, Axes, int]:
1145        """
1146
1147        Plots the time series of all motor unit potentials of one motor unit in one
1148        channel, with the mean time series overlaid. MUP onset is plotted at t = 0 ms.
1149
1150        If channel is not specified, the channel used for detecting motor unit
1151        potentials is plotted.
1152
1153        Note that the channel is specified using the channel index (counting from 0),
1154        not the channel numeric label (counting from 1).
1155
1156        Parameters
1157        ----------
1158        motor_unit_idx : int
1159            Index of motor unit in EMGMotorUnits class for which to extract the
1160            potential time series data.
1161        chan_idx : int, optional
1162            Index of the channel to plot. The default is None,
1163            which gives the channel used to find motor units.
1164        n_ms : int, optional
1165            Number of milliseconds of data to extract. The data will be centered on the
1166            motor unit potential's onset. The default is 20.
1167        lw : float, optional
1168            Line width of the individual traces. The default is 1.
1169        alpha : float, optional
1170            Alpha of individual traces. The default is 0.25.
1171        clr: Any, optional
1172            Colour of the individual traces (e.g., as string or RGB tuple). The default
1173            is "darkgrey".
1174        lw_mean : float, optional
1175            Line width of mean line. The default is 2.
1176        alpha_mean : float, optional
1177            Alpha of the mean line. The default is 0.75.
1178        clr_mean : Any, optional
1179            Colour of the mean trace (e.g., as string or RGB tuple). The default
1180            is "black".
1181        figsize : tuple[float, float], optional
1182            Size of figure. The default is (7, 7).
1183        axis_label_size : float, optional
1184            Size of axis labels. The default is 12.
1185        title_size : float, optional
1186            Font size the titles. The default is 12.
1187        xtick_label_size : float, optional
1188            size of x tick labels. The default is 10.
1189        ytick_label_size : float, optional
1190            Size of y tick labels. The default is 10.
1191        dpi : int, optional
1192            Dots per Inch. The default is 100.
1193        ax : plt.axes.Axes, optional
1194            Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
1195
1196        Raises
1197        ------
1198        ValueError
1199            Checks motor units exist.
1200
1201        Returns
1202        -------
1203        fig : Figure
1204            The figure to which the plot belongs.
1205        ax : Axes
1206            The axes to which the plot belongs.
1207        chan_idx : int
1208            Channel used to plot the fibre potentials.
1209
1210        """
1211
1212        if not self.found_motor_units:
1213            raise ValueError("No motor units identified - confirm that analysis has been run.")
1214
1215        if chan_idx < 0:
1216            chan_idx = self.chan_for_find_motor_units
1217
1218        # Create new figure with specified size if no axis provided.
1219        if ax is None:
1220            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
1221            fig.dpi = dpi
1222        else:
1223            fig = None
1224
1225        # Get motor unit potentials and average (mean).
1226        potentials_data = self._get_potentials_data_of_one_motor_unit(motor_unit_idx, n_ms)
1227        potentials_avg = np.nanmean(potentials_data, axis=2)
1228        n_samples = potentials_avg.shape[1]
1229
1230        # Time vector for x axis (ms)
1231        potentials_t = (np.arange(1, n_samples + 1) / self.emg_data_preproc.fs) * 1000
1232        potentials_t = potentials_t - n_ms / 2  # Center MUP so onset is at t = 0 ms
1233
1234        # Plot each MUP in specified channel.
1235        ax.plot(
1236            potentials_t,
1237            np.squeeze(potentials_data[chan_idx, :, :]),
1238            lw=lw,
1239            color=clr,
1240            alpha=alpha,
1241            label="_nolegend_",
1242        )
1243        ax.plot(
1244            potentials_t,
1245            potentials_avg[chan_idx, :],
1246            lw=lw_mean,
1247            color=clr_mean,
1248            alpha=alpha_mean,
1249            label="mean potential",
1250        )
1251        ax.legend(loc="lower left", frameon=False)
1252
1253        # Labels
1254        ax.tick_params(axis="y", which="major", labelsize=ytick_label_size)
1255        ax.set_ylabel("\u03bcV", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1256
1257        # x-axis labels and font size.
1258        ax.set_xlabel("time (ms)", fontsize=axis_label_size)
1259        ax.tick_params(axis="x", which="major", labelsize=xtick_label_size)
1260        ax.set_xlim(0 - n_ms / 2, max(potentials_t))
1261
1262        # Title
1263        ax.set_title(
1264            f"Average potential (across time) of motor unit {motor_unit_idx + 1}"
1265            + f" in channel {chan_idx}",
1266            fontweight="bold",
1267            fontsize=title_size,
1268        )
1269
1270        return fig, ax, chan_idx

Plots the time series of all motor unit potentials of one motor unit in one channel, with the mean time series overlaid. MUP onset is plotted at t = 0 ms.

If channel is not specified, the channel used for detecting motor unit potentials is plotted.

Note that the channel is specified using the channel index (counting from 0), not the channel numeric label (counting from 1).

Parameters
  • motor_unit_idx (int): Index of motor unit in EMGMotorUnits class for which to extract the potential time series data.
  • chan_idx (int, optional): Index of the channel to plot. The default is None, which gives the channel used to find motor units.
  • n_ms (int, optional): Number of milliseconds of data to extract. The data will be centered on the motor unit potential's onset. The default is 20.
  • lw (float, optional): Line width of the individual traces. The default is 1.
  • alpha (float, optional): Alpha of individual traces. The default is 0.25.
  • clr (Any, optional): Colour of the individual traces (e.g., as string or RGB tuple). The default is "darkgrey".
  • lw_mean (float, optional): Line width of mean line. The default is 2.
  • alpha_mean (float, optional): Alpha of the mean line. The default is 0.75.
  • clr_mean (Any, optional): Colour of the mean trace (e.g., as string or RGB tuple). The default is "black".
  • figsize (tuple[float, float], optional): Size of figure. The default is (7, 7).
  • axis_label_size (float, optional): Size of axis labels. The default is 12.
  • title_size (float, optional): Font size the titles. The default is 12.
  • xtick_label_size (float, optional): size of x tick labels. The default is 10.
  • ytick_label_size (float, optional): Size of y tick labels. The default is 10.
  • dpi (int, optional): Dots per Inch. The default is 100.
  • ax (plt.axes.Axes, optional): Plot to add to. The default is None, in which case new axes are created.
Raises
  • ValueError: Checks motor units exist.
Returns
  • fig (Figure): The figure to which the plot belongs.
  • ax (Axes): The axes to which the plot belongs.
  • chan_idx (int): Channel used to plot the fibre potentials.
def reconstruct_fibres(self, motor_unit_number: int): 
1272    def reconstruct_fibres(self, motor_unit_number: int):
1273        """
1274        Fills in fibre construction data and stores it
1275        in the corresponding motor unit object.
1276
1277        Parameters
1278        ----------
1279        motor_unit_number: int
1280            motor unit number used as a label.
1281
1282        Returns
1283        -------
1284        None.
1285
1286        """
1287
1288        # Motor unit for this number.
1289        motor_unit = self.found_motor_units.motor_units[motor_unit_number]
1290
1291        # Save the concurrent signal from all other channels for each spike.
1292        all_spikes = np.zeros(
1293            (
1294                len(motor_unit.potentials_t_idx),
1295                self.n_chan,
1296                self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size * 2 + 1,
1297            )
1298        )
1299
1300        # MU firings count.
1301        t = 0
1302
1303        for t_idx in motor_unit.potentials_t_idx:
1304            # exclude spikes right at the edge of the recording.
1305            if t_idx < (self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size + 1) or t_idx > (
1306                self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts.shape[1]
1307                - self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size
1308                - 1
1309                - 1
1310            ):
1311                continue
1312
1313            for channel in range(self.n_chan):
1314                # Skip bad channels
1315                if not self.emg_data_preproc.chan.analyse_chan[channel]:
1316                    continue
1317
1318                all_spikes[t, channel, :] = self.emg_data_preproc.emg_ts[
1319                    channel,
1320                    int(t_idx - self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size) : int(
1321                        t_idx + self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size + 1
1322                    ),
1323                ]
1324
1325            t += 1
1326
1327        print("Motor Unit " + str(motor_unit_number + 1) + ": firings: " + str(t))
1328
1329        if self.recon_settings.mavg_all:
1330            self.recon_settings.mavg_length = all_spikes.shape[0] - 1
1331        elif t < self.recon_settings.mavg_length or t < 2:
1332            # if there aren't enough spikes to model the MU, skip it.
1333            print("Too few firings found to model this motor unit")
1334            return
1335
1336        # The x, y coordinates of the fibre potential.
1337        pos = np.zeros((0, 2))
1338        # Onset indices of the MUPs (firings) relative to the overall time.
1339        mup_onsets = np.array([])
1340        # Fibre potential peak times relative to the onset time
1341        # of the corresponding MUP (in indices units).
1342        fibre_potential_times = np.array([])
1343
1344        # Fibre potential peak channels
1345        fibre_potential_peak_chan = np.array([])
1346
1347        max_signal_id = all_spikes.shape[0] - self.recon_settings.mavg_length
1348
1349        # Loop thro' MUPs.
1350        for signal_id in range(max_signal_id):
1351            sig = np.squeeze(
1352                np.mean(
1353                    all_spikes[
1354                        signal_id : (signal_id + self.recon_settings.mavg_length + 1),
1355                        :,
1356                        :,
1357                    ],
1358                    axis=0,
1359                )
1360            )
1361
1362            # Find peaks in 2D array, channels x time.
1363            sub_clusters = self._find_peaks_2d(sig)
1364
1365            if sub_clusters.shape[0] == 0:
1366                continue
1367
1368            # Each peak found above defines a fibre potential. The positions are now
1369            # calculated (estimated) relative to the needle electrodes.
1370            for sub_cluster_index in range(sub_clusters.shape[0]):
1371                # Ensure we don't get spikes outside of recording duration.
1372                time_peak = np.max(
1373                    np.hstack(
1374                        (
1375                            sub_clusters[sub_cluster_index, 0],
1376                            self.recon_settings.spike_dur + 1,
1377                        )
1378                    )
1379                )
1380                time_peak = np.min(
1381                    np.hstack(
1382                        (
1383                            time_peak,
1384                            self.recon_settings.half_subsample_size * 2
1385                            - self.recon_settings.spike_dur,
1386                        )
1387                    )
1388                )
1389
1390                # Get the mean spikes for the fibre peak amplitude.
1391                peak_electrode = sub_clusters[sub_cluster_index, 1]
1392                peak_start = np.max(np.hstack((peak_electrode - 3, 0)))
1393                peak_stop = np.min(np.hstack((peak_electrode + 3, self.n_chan - 1)))
1394
1395                included_electrodes = np.arange(peak_start, peak_stop + 1, dtype="int")
1396
1397                # Remove bad channels.
1398                good_channels = (
1399                    np.arange(0, self.n_chan, dtype="int")
1400                    * self.emg_data_preproc.chan.analyse_chan
1401                )
1402                included_electrodes = np.intersect1d(included_electrodes, good_channels)
1403
1404                if included_electrodes.shape[0] == 0:
1405                    continue
1406
1407                self.sn = (
1408                    sig[
1409                        included_electrodes,
1410                        int(time_peak - self.recon_settings.spike_dur) : int(
1411                            time_peak + self.recon_settings.spike_dur + 1
1412                        ),
1413                    ]
1414                ).T
1415
1416                self.needle = self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_xy
1417                x0 = self.needle[int(peak_electrode), :]
1418                self.needle = self.needle[included_electrodes, :]
1419
1420                # Non-linear optimisation algorithm for fibre positioning.
1421                opt_paras = opt.fmin(
1422                    self._deconv_wrapper,
1423                    x0=x0,
1424                    maxiter=self.recon_settings.max_opt_iterations,
1425                    full_output=False,
1426                    xtol=self.recon_settings.xtol,
1427                    ftol=self.recon_settings.ftol,
1428                    disp=False,
1429                )
1430
1431                pos = np.vstack((pos, opt_paras))
1432
1433                mup_onsets = np.append(mup_onsets, motor_unit.potentials_t_idx[signal_id])
1434
1435                # Add fibre potential times, these are already adjusted
1436                #  and relative to the MUP onset times.
1437                fibre_potential_times = np.append(fibre_potential_times, time_peak)
1438
1439                # Add fibre peak channel
1440                fibre_potential_peak_chan = np.append(fibre_potential_peak_chan, peak_electrode)
1441
1442        # End of signal_id loop.
1443
1444        # Scaling factor to account for tissue attenuation differences in y-axis direction.
1445        pos[:, 1] = pos[:, 1] * self.recon_settings.y_scaling_factor
1446
1447        # Add the results to the motor unit object.
1448        if pos.shape[0] > 0:
1449            motor_unit.add_fibre_localisation(
1450                fibre_centres=pos,
1451                mup_onsets=mup_onsets,
1452                fibre_potential_times=fibre_potential_times,
1453                fibre_potential_peak_chan=fibre_potential_peak_chan,
1454                all_spikes=all_spikes,
1455                generator_potential=np.array(np.transpose(self.opr)),
1456            )
1457
1458        # Restore needle to full needle, rather than subset of the needle.
1459        self.needle = self.emg_data_preproc.chan.chan_xy
